# Security

Security is built-in, not bolted-on. Every feature, endpoint, and data flow must consider security implications.

## OWASP Top 10 (2025)

| #   | Vulnerability                      | Prevention                                      |
| --- | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | Broken Access Control              | Verify permissions server-side, default deny    |
| 2   | Security Misconfiguration          | Secure defaults, remove unused features         |
| 3   | Software Supply Chain Failures     | SBOM, dependency scanning, signed builds        |
| 4   | Cryptographic Failures             | Use TLS, hash passwords (argon2id), encrypt PII |
| 5   | Injection                          | Parameterized queries, input validation         |
| 6   | Insecure Design                    | Threat modeling, security requirements          |
| 7   | Authentication Failures            | Strong passwords, MFA, secure session mgmt      |
| 8   | Software or Data Integrity         | Verify dependencies, sign releases              |
| 9   | Logging and Alerting Failures      | Log security events, set up alerts              |
| 10  | Mishandling Exceptional Conditions | Fail securely, generic errors to clients        |

## Security Principles

| Principle          | Rule                                                      |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Defense in Depth   | Multiple layers: firewall, auth, authz, encryption, audit |
| Least Privilege    | Minimum permissions needed, nothing more                  |
| Zero Trust         | Never trust, always verify. Assume breach.                |
| Secure by Default  | HTTPS, strict passwords, secure cookies out of the box    |
| Fail Securely      | Access denied on error, no internal details to users      |
| Validate on Server | Client validation is UX, server validation is security    |

## Pre-Deployment Checklist

| Area          | Requirements                                                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Passwords     | Hashed with argon2id (preferred) or bcrypt (12+ rounds)             |
| Tokens        | JWT with EdDSA/ES256, 15min access / 7d refresh, httpOnly cookies   |
| Sessions      | HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies                           |
| Rate Limiting | Auth endpoints: 5 attempts/15min                                    |
| Authorization | All routes check auth server-side, default deny                     |
| Input         | Validated with schema (Zod), parameterized SQL                      |
| Uploads       | Whitelist types, enforce size limits                                |
| Secrets       | No secrets in code or VCS                                           |
| Headers       | CSP (with nonces), HSTS, Permissions-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options |
| CORS          | Configured restrictively                                            |
| Encryption    | PII encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3)            |
| Logging       | Audit logging for security events                                   |
| Dependencies  | SBOM generated, `npm audit` clean, Dependabot enabled               |

## Threat Modeling (STRIDE)

| Threat                 | Category        | Key Mitigations                                        |
| ---------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Spoofing               | Authentication  | MFA, strong passwords, JWT with short expiry           |
| Tampering              | Integrity       | Input validation, HTTPS/TLS, signed tokens             |
| Repudiation            | Accountability  | Audit logging, digital signatures                      |

# Security

| #   | Vulnerability                      | Prevention                                      |

| 1   | Broken Access Control              | Verify permissions server-side, default deny    |
| 2   | Security Misconfiguration          | Secure defaults, remove unused features         |

| 4   | Cryptographic Failures             | Use TLS, hash passwords (argon2id), encrypt PII |

| 6   | Insecure Design                    | Threat modeling, security requirements          |
| 7   | Authentication Failures            | Strong passwords, MFA, secure session mgmt      |
| 8   | Software or Data Integrity         | Verify dependencies, sign releases              |
| 9   | Logging and Alerting Failures      | Log security events, set up alerts              |
| 10  | Mishandling Exceptional Conditions | Fail securely, generic errors to clients        |

## Security Principles

| Principle          | Rule                                                      |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Defense in Depth   | Multiple layers: firewall, auth, authz, encryption, audit |
| Least Privilege    | Minimum permissions needed, nothing more                  |
| Zero Trust         | Never trust, always verify. Assume breach.                |
| Secure by Default  | HTTPS, strict passwords, secure cookies out of the box    |
| Fail Securely      | Access denied on error, no internal details to users      |

| Headers       | CSP (with nonces), HSTS, Permissions-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options |

This is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

completion(prompt, model?="default"|"smol"|"slow", system?=None, schema?=None) → handle; `.wait()` returns text (parsed with `schema`). Stateless, no tools/history.
await judge(state, questions, images?=[path | ImageContent, …]) → `{id: answer}`
    Typed judgment over one `state` (str | JSON object | JSON array). Every question sees the same state and is answered independently: batch independent questions into one call. Cheap and fast (TypeSafe when credentialed, else the tiny/smol chat model); prefer over `completion()` for classification, yes/no, ranking. Two or more states → `judge_batch`, never a loop of `judge()`.
    `questions`: `{id: q}` where q is one of
      `{type: "choice", instructions, criteria: {label: rubric | None, …}}` → `{choice, probabilities: {label: p}, confidence}` (≥2 labels)
      `{type: "bool", instructions, criteria?: {true?: str, false?: str}}` → `{bool: P(yes)}`
      `{type: "score", instructions, criteria: [lowest, …, highest]}` → `{score, probabilities: {"0": p, …}, confidence}` (≥2 levels; score is the probability-weighted level index)
judge_batch(states, questions, concurrency?=32, retries?=1, min_ok?=1, intent?=None, images?={key: [path | ImageContent, …]}) → JudgmentBatch
    Images accept local paths or embedded `ImageContent`; batch attachments map each state key to its list (array inputs use zero-based index keys). Image requests skip candidates without image support, never silently drop images, and fail if no compatible judge remains.
    Same `questions` over every state (`{key: state}` or a list keyed by index), run and owned by the host — it outlives the cell. `intent` is an optional nonempty progress/job label (default `"Judging"`). Returns at once; pull settled items in bounded slices across cells: `await b.drain(timeout?)` → `[(key, item)]` settled since the last drain (`[]` on timeout; `item.answers` on success, else `item.error`, never raised); `async for k, item in b.drain_iter(timeout)` until timeout or completion; `b.status()` → `{intent, done, total, failed, cost, running, model}`; `b.results()` → `{key: answers}` so far; `b.failed()` → `{key: error}`; `b.cancel()`; `b.close()` releases it. `drain()` raises only when the run died wholesale (no judge, or fewer than `min_ok` answered). `b.id` is an async job id: completion auto-delivers a summary, `wait` blocks when you have nothing else to do, `judge_batch.attach(id)` re-creates the ref after a reset.
```

209:### What a persona migration actually needs to map
210:
211:[specialist.rs][E9] shows that current consultations do more than append a static role: they validate the persona/verb, resolve the caller's route and mode, select a memory namespace, assemble dynamic persona pieces and scoped context, add role/knowledge, preserve the operation in the prompt, recheck admission, invoke provider-only completion and construct typed persona/source metadata.

It has **no direct `system_prompt` field**. `IdentityConfig` supports OpenClaw/AIEOS documents and AIEOS inline/file sources. These establish native configuration mechanisms, not a completed translation of our prompt assembly.

215:**OD-122 proposal:** move static role/knowledge into appropriate native identity/bundle facilities where useful; map verbs, dynamic context and result metadata separately. Do not make exact reproduction of all 567 legacy method names a prerequisite for the first consolidation slice. Do not silently change provider-only consultation into tool-enabled agent execution.

217:**OD-123 proposal:** retain Cozo ownership and scope. The mounted `AgentMemoryConfig.backend` defaults to `sqlite`; `MemoryBackendKind` declares none/sqlite/postgres/qdrant/markdown/lucid, with no Cozo option. That is a concrete future integration gap. It is not authorization to add SQL/SQLite, switch stores, migrate data or silently disable memory. Other consolidation can proceed while this work stays on the wishlist.

# Mastering System Consolidation — grounded implementation brief
…
## 3. What to consolidate
…
### Coverage of the rest of the catalog
…

## 4. Native capture and the schema-to-blob boundary

The present implementation is:

1. Explicit `opblob` sealing calls `threetched::prepare_schema_capture`.
2. The selected binary/manifest are checked; the capture reads native `config schema`, recursive command `--help`, version and binary digest.
3. `schema_from_capture` derives the threetched PluginSchema. Separately registered handwritten plugins still produce their own PluginSchemas.
4. `opblob` seals each full PluginSchema into the blob catalog. Full reseal removes plugin IDs absent from the build.
5. Golden preparation stages the already sealed catalog; snapshot send/receive and activation transport it. FUSE projects the resulting declarations and committed state.

Evidence: [explicit sealer][E13], [capture owner][E14], [CLI capture implementation][E15], [full-schema blob serialization][E16]. Duplicate authoring enters **before sealing**; a shared catalog alone does not remove it.

### Capture gaps and concrete evidence

| Area | Grounded evidence | Work needed for a selected implementation slice |
|---|---|---|
| Native HTTP config | Pinned gateway `openapi.rs::build_spec` derives schemas from native Rust types; gateway declares `/api/openapi.json`. `api_config.rs` defines property/list/patch/init/migrate types and errors. | Import the relevant native-owned contract with provenance. Do not assume the current CLI capture already includes HTTP results/errors. |
| OpenAPI coverage | The inspected source includes config/version paths, `/api/skills/slash-option-kinds`, additional schema components, and a feature-gated A2A addition. It is not an export of every gateway or WebSocket operation. | Inventory actual exported coverage. Earlier shorthand “config/version only” was incomplete; neither that shorthand nor the generated lesson is sufficient authority for coverage. |
| Native tools | Current adapter reads `/api/tools`: name, description, parameters and optional output. Its local type deliberately omits native `param_domains`. | Preserve needed native metadata when deriving the chosen methods. Agent/config-dependent tool visibility must not turn a capture identity's tools into universal grants. |
| Cron | Source declares `/api/cron`, `/api/cron/{id}`, `/api/cron/{id}/runs` and `/api/cron/{id}/run`. | Use these verified paths. The lesson's `/cron/history` and `/cron/run` are not the inspected routes. |
| Provider-only generation | Pinned patch exposes `/ws/chat?stateless_generation=1`, protocol `tched_router.generation.v1`, strict connect/message inputs and session_start/connected/chunk/done/error outputs. | Export/derive the native frame contract for the generation slice. No existing `threetched.Chat` method should be assumed. |
| Cancellation and receipts | Native stateless code drops the provider stream on disconnect and notes that the remote provider may already have accepted input. Local `cancel_generation` checks job revision, commits state and signals a worker. | Preserve truthful cancellation/state outcomes. Do not describe the local job method as an already exported native cancellation frame, or assume disconnect undoes provider effects. |

Sources: [pinned source archive and recipe][E17], archive members `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/openapi.rs` (build_spec at line 58, routes at 204 onward), `api_config.rs`, `lib.rs` (config/tool/cron registrations at 1658–1980); [native tools adapter][E18]; [generation patch][E19]; [generation jobs][E12]. These are source observations, not live endpoint calls.

**Proposed implementation rule:** extend the existing explicit authoring/capture boundary and, where necessary, the pinned native export. Derive selected operations from native types/exports; retain binary, patch, version and schema provenance. Runtime consumers continue to use the sealed catalog. Do not add another repository `schemas/` authority, live schema fallback, generic parallel API client or second control plane. Unsupported capture remains an explicit gap or deferred feature.

Do not require complete HTTP/tool/WebSocket capture before removing the already captured plugin/skill wrappers. Capture becomes necessary when a selected migration depends on the missing contract.

## 5. Cognitive: complete counts and a bounded proposal

| Group | Methods | Current evidence / disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| Persona consultations | 567 | 81 personas × seven verbs. Shared native inference; persona/config improvements deferred under OD-122. |
| Execution catalog | 59 | 12 aliases backed by five executors. Existing dispatch uses identity-bearing `UnifiedExecution` D-Bus calls. Native shell/runtime overlap is a candidate, not proven language-operation equivalence. |
| Orchestration catalog | 18 | Six agents × three operations. Each child goes through canonical admission with the original caller. Native SOP/pipeline comparison may be deferred. |
| Memory operations | 7 | `memory_store/retrieve/query/recall/delete/list_namespaces/semantic_query`. Existing scoped Cozo owner, optional Qdrant semantics. OD-123 covers future native integration. |
| Code retrieval/indexing | 3 | `code_search`, `code_context`, `code_index`: Voyage/Qdrant and session-aware context. Generic native project/memory sections do not establish equivalent retrieval. |
| Compatibility agent facades | 6 | `rust_pro`, `python_pro`, `typescript_pro`, `sequential_thinking`, `context_manager`, `code_review_orchestrator`. |
| Workflow facades | 2 | `workflow_query/run`, sharing the local workstack owner. |
| Specialist/provider calls | 2 | `specialist` plus `gemini_query`; the latter has separate provider/research behavior. |
| Discovery/admission/policy | 6 | `get_health`, `list_tools`, `invoke_tool`, `schema_read`, `oscal_subids`, `toolsets`. |
| **Total** | **670** | **644 agent methods + 26 other methods.** |

The lesson's abbreviated list totaled 660. Persona consultations alone are **84.6%** of 670, not “over 85%.” These are generated declarations from [agent descriptors][E20], not 567 independently handwritten function implementations. The opportunity is reducing duplicate exposed contracts and local behavior that native facilities can own.

### What a persona migration actually needs to map

[specialist.rs][E9] shows that current consultations do more than append a static role: they validate the persona/verb, resolve the caller's route and mode, select a memory namespace, assemble dynamic persona pieces and scoped context, add role/knowledge, preserve the operation in the prompt, recheck admission, invoke provider-only completion and construct typed persona/source metadata.

The mounted Config's `AliasedAgentConfig` supports `identity`, `knowledge_bundles`, `skill_bundles`, `model_provider`, `risk_profile`, `runtime_profile`, `workspace`, `memory` and related fields. It has **no direct `system_prompt` field**. `IdentityConfig` supports OpenClaw/AIEOS documents and AIEOS inline/file sources. These establish native configuration mechanisms, not a completed translation of our prompt assembly.

**OD-122 proposal:** move static role/knowledge into appropriate native identity/bundle facilities where useful; map verbs, dynamic context and result metadata separately. Do not make exact reproduction of all 567 legacy method names a prerequisite for the first consolidation slice. Do not silently change provider-only consultation into tool-enabled agent execution.

**OD-123 proposal:** retain Cozo ownership and scope. The mounted `AgentMemoryConfig.backend` defaults to `sqlite`; `MemoryBackendKind` declares none/sqlite/postgres/qdrant/markdown/lucid, with no Cozo option. That is a concrete future integration gap. It is not authorization to add SQL/SQLite, switch stores, migrate data or silently disable memory. Other consolidation can proceed while this work stays on the wishlist.

Evidence: [mounted Config inside the native schema][E1], [specialist context/completion][E9], [execution dispatch][E21], [workflow admission][E22]. No agent configuration or memory backend was changed while preparing this brief.

## 6. Dependencies the implementing LLM must reconcile

| Dependency | Required treatment |
|---|---|
| Callers | Trace exact plugin/method references through bridge dispatch, UI, schema loaders, toolsets and generated outputs. Inspect the sibling UI's `src/chat/{door-chat-adapter,native-routing,control-plane-model,router-committed-route}.ts` and `src/grpc/door.ts`; do not assume one file handles every caller. Update the pinned UI input when the changed UI is part of a release. |
| Schema ownership | Make native operation shapes derive from the one native contract. Local policy/receipt integration must not independently reauthor native arguments/results. Never invent the target method name because the old owner used it. |
| State | Identify existing public/private state and child objects before changing owner paths. Preserve principal/session scope, unrelated children and authoritative Cozo data. Commit actual backend results to canonical SHM before notifications. Do not assume a global rename to `threetched` preserves state isolation. |
| Capability mapping | Build explicit old-method → canonical-operation → exact-capability mappings. Read/write distinctions, actor/session admission and current grants must survive. A hashed CLI capability is not automatically equivalent to an old typed read capability. No wildcard grants or direct policy rewrites to hide denials. |
| Receipts/errors | Distinguish execution failure, backend acceptance, state-publication failure, cancellation and recovery. A successful filesystem write or CLI exit alone is not proof of the full operation. |
| Mount selection | The host adapter currently hardcodes `threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills`. Update it consistently with actual catalog removals. Preserve our/upstream naming and separation. [Adapter source][E23]. |
| Generated/release inputs | Remove obsolete module/registry/dispatch references, regenerate affected derived views through existing mechanisms, prepare an isolated catalog, review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs and stage the matching binaries/config/UI. Do not hand-edit generated output as a second authority. |

For capability changes, preserving existing authorization is not permission to broaden it. Follow the repository's smallest-concrete-change procedure if a genuinely new grant is required. An operation denial is evidence to diagnose, not a reason to switch identities or transports.

## 7. Implementation sequence and completion evidence

This is a proposed sequence for the receiving agent. The owner asked this author to produce a prompt/document, not execute the application changes.

1. **Reconcile the shared work first.** Read current AGENTS/HANDOFF/SIGNALS and the mounted catalog. Two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source before the mapping hold, with related edits in `mod.rs`, `threetched.rs` and `mutation_engine.rs`; those removals remain unbuilt/unsealed/undeployed. Preserve unrelated work and finish this slice coherently rather than restarting it.
2. **Finish the directly captured wrapper slice.** Resolve plugin/skill command inputs, outputs, capabilities and callers against the 18 native commands. Reconcile mount selections and generated inputs. Record any feature deliberately retired/deferred instead of introducing replacement duplicate schemas.
3. **Migrate further proven overlaps in dependency order.** Select the next useful config/provider/cron/router subset. Add only the native capture needed by that subset; retain required local admission/state/receipt integration. Do not hold the first slice for full persona, memory or workflow parity.
4. **Build and prepare the release inputs.** Follow JEV's Cargo routing, one Cargo process, native `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, release `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`. Use the freshly built `opblob` for an isolated `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>` catalog with matching schema-shaping environment. Review removals and preserve recovery inputs. Golden consumes the already sealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.
5. **Hand off with exact status.** Report changed files, implemented/retired/deferred methods, build result, catalog delta, remaining blockers and next action. Live deployment, when explicitly included in the receiving task, uses `./activate-golden.sh` and snapshot send/receive; never hand-copy application binaries into the running host. Track host mount wiring separately from the application snapshot.

Evidence for a completed implementation slice includes resolved callers, one schema owner, exact catalog delta, successful required build and consistent release inputs. If deployed, add native activation/readiness receipts, mount/catalog agreement and resulting authoritative state where an admitted operation is available. Missing identity provisioning or an unavailable operation remains an explicit limitation.

**Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures remain owner-request-only.** The NotebookLM `cargo check --workspace` and persona-test gates are not automatic authority to run checks. Workspace scope and build execution follow the receiving prompt and current AGENTS. Report unrun tests as unrun. There is no claim of zero risk, guaranteed zero downtime or complete semantic parity.

Existing guard/storage holds and later subvolume pinning remain outside this scope. Future lungs MCP is neither a dependency of the first consolidation slice nor an interface to implement now.

## 8. What is ready to hand off

- **Grounded baseline:** mounted counts, real method names, native Config fields, current source ownership and the actual cron/generation/tool contract evidence.
- **First implementation slice:** finish the existing plugin/skill-wrapper removal and reconcile callers, mount selection, generated inputs and release catalog.
- **Subsequent slices:** migrate proven native overlap as needed contracts become available; track selected behavior and dependencies explicitly.
- **Deferred enhancements:** OD-122 native persona/configuration mapping; OD-123 Cozo-backed native memory integration. These do not block unrelated consolidation.
- **Current authoring status:** documentation and task-board changes only; no new application implementation, build, seal, deployment, grants, mounts or storage changes.

The implementation prompt is at the top of this file. The receiving LLM must reread present sources and shared ownership; this evidence is dated, not a substitute for current state.

170:4. `opblob` seals each full PluginSchema into the blob catalog. Full reseal removes plugin IDs absent from the build.
171:5. Golden preparation stages the already sealed catalog; snapshot send/receive and activation transport it. FUSE projects the resulting declarations and committed state.

Do not assume the current CLI capture already includes HTTP results/errors. |

It is not an export of every gateway or WebSocket operation. | Inventory actual exported coverage. Earlier shorthand “config/version only” was incomplete; neither that shorthand nor the generated lesson is sufficient authority for coverage. |

Its local type deliberately omits native `param_domains`. | Preserve needed native metadata when deriving the chosen methods. Agent/config-dependent tool visibility must not turn a capture identity's tools into universal grants. |

194:| Group | Methods | Current evidence / disposition |

197:| Execution catalog | 59 | 12 aliases backed by five executors. Existing dispatch uses identity-bearing `UnifiedExecution` D-Bus calls. Native shell/runtime overlap is a candidate, not proven language-operation equivalence. |

Persona consultations alone are **84.6%** of 670, not “over 85%.” These are generated declarations from [agent descriptors][E20], not 567 independently handwritten function implementations. The opportunity is reducing duplicate exposed contracts and local behavior that native facilities can own.

209:### What a persona migration actually needs to map
210:
211:[specialist.rs][E9] shows that current consultations do more than append a static role: they validate the persona/verb, resolve the caller's route and mode, select a memory namespace, assemble dynamic persona pieces and scoped context, add role/knowledge, preserve the operation in the prompt, recheck admission, invoke provider-only completion and construct typed persona/source metadata.
212:
213:The mounted Config's `AliasedAgentConfig` supports `identity`, `knowledge_bundles`, `skill_bundles`, `model_provider`, `risk_profile`, `runtime_profile`, `workspace`, `memory` and related fields. It has **no direct `system_prompt` field**. `IdentityConfig` supports OpenClaw/AIEOS documents and AIEOS inline/file sources. These establish native configuration mechanisms, not a completed translation of our prompt assembly.
214:
215:**OD-122 proposal:** move static role/knowledge into appropriate native identity/bundle facilities where useful; map verbs, dynamic context and result metadata separately. Do not make exact reproduction of all 567 legacy method names a prerequisite for the first consolidation slice. Do not silently change provider-only consultation into tool-enabled agent execution.
216:
217:**OD-123 proposal:** retain Cozo ownership and scope. The mounted `AgentMemoryConfig.backend` defaults to `sqlite`; `MemoryBackendKind` declares none/sqlite/postgres/qdrant/markdown/lucid, with no Cozo option. That is a concrete future integration gap. It is not authorization to add SQL/SQLite, switch stores, migrate data or silently disable memory. Other consolidation can proceed while this work stays on the wishlist.

Inspect the sibling UI's `src/chat/{door-chat-adapter,native-routing,control-plane-model,router-committed-route}.ts` and `src/grpc/door.ts`; do not assume one file handles every caller. Update the pinned UI input when the changed UI is part of a release. |
226:| Schema ownership | Make native operation shapes derive from the one native contract. Local policy/receipt integration must not independently reauthor native arguments/results. Never invent the target method name because the old owner used it. |
227:| State | Identify existing public/private state and child objects before changing owner paths. Preserve principal/session scope, unrelated children and authoritative Cozo data. Commit actual backend results to canonical SHM before notifications. Do not assume a global rename to `threetched` preserves state isolation. |
228:| Capability mapping | Build explicit old-method → canonical-operation → exact-capability mappings. Read/write distinctions, actor/session admission and current grants must survive. A hashed CLI capability is not automatically equivalent to an old typed read capability. No wildcard grants or direct policy rewrites to hide denials. |

231:| Generated/release inputs | Remove obsolete module/registry/dispatch references, regenerate affected derived views through existing mechanisms, prepare an isolated catalog, review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs and stage the matching binaries/config/UI. Do not hand-edit generated output as a second authority. |

233:For capability changes, preserving existing authorization is not permission to broaden it. Follow the repository's smallest-concrete-change procedure if a genuinely new grant is required. An operation denial is evidence to diagnose, not a reason to switch identities or transports.

# Mastering System Consolidation — grounded implementation brief
…
## 3. What to consolidate
…
### Coverage of the rest of the catalog
…

## 4. Native capture and the schema-to-blob boundary

The present implementation is:

1. Explicit `opblob` sealing calls `threetched::prepare_schema_capture`.
2. The selected binary/manifest are checked; the capture reads native `config schema`, recursive command `--help`, version and binary digest.
3. `schema_from_capture` derives the threetched PluginSchema. Separately registered handwritten plugins still produce their own PluginSchemas.
4. `opblob` seals each full PluginSchema into the blob catalog. Full reseal removes plugin IDs absent from the build.
5. Golden preparation stages the already sealed catalog; snapshot send/receive and activation transport it. FUSE projects the resulting declarations and committed state.

Evidence: [explicit sealer][E13], [capture owner][E14], [CLI capture implementation][E15], [full-schema blob serialization][E16]. Duplicate authoring enters **before sealing**; a shared catalog alone does not remove it.

### Capture gaps and concrete evidence

| Area | Grounded evidence | Work needed for a selected implementation slice |
|---|---|---|
| Native HTTP config | Pinned gateway `openapi.rs::build_spec` derives schemas from native Rust types; gateway declares `/api/openapi.json`. `api_config.rs` defines property/list/patch/init/migrate types and errors. | Import the relevant native-owned contract with provenance. Do not assume the current CLI capture already includes HTTP results/errors. |
| OpenAPI coverage | The inspected source includes config/version paths, `/api/skills/slash-option-kinds`, additional schema components, and a feature-gated A2A addition. It is not an export of every gateway or WebSocket operation. | Inventory actual exported coverage. Earlier shorthand “config/version only” was incomplete; neither that shorthand nor the generated lesson is sufficient authority for coverage. |
| Native tools | Current adapter reads `/api/tools`: name, description, parameters and optional output. Its local type deliberately omits native `param_domains`. | Preserve needed native metadata when deriving the chosen methods. Agent/config-dependent tool visibility must not turn a capture identity's tools into universal grants. |
| Cron | Source declares `/api/cron`, `/api/cron/{id}`, `/api/cron/{id}/runs` and `/api/cron/{id}/run`. | Use these verified paths. The lesson's `/cron/history` and `/cron/run` are not the inspected routes. |
| Provider-only generation | Pinned patch exposes `/ws/chat?stateless_generation=1`, protocol `tched_router.generation.v1`, strict connect/message inputs and session_start/connected/chunk/done/error outputs. | Export/derive the native frame contract for the generation slice. No existing `threetched.Chat` method should be assumed. |
| Cancellation and receipts | Native stateless code drops the provider stream on disconnect and notes that the remote provider may already have accepted input. Local `cancel_generation` checks job revision, commits state and signals a worker. | Preserve truthful cancellation/state outcomes. Do not describe the local job method as an already exported native cancellation frame, or assume disconnect undoes provider effects. |

Sources: [pinned source archive and recipe][E17], archive members `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/openapi.rs` (build_spec at line 58, routes at 204 onward), `api_config.rs`, `lib.rs` (config/tool/cron registrations at 1658–1980); [native tools adapter][E18]; [generation patch][E19]; [generation jobs][E12]. These are source observations, not live endpoint calls.

**Proposed implementation rule:** extend the existing explicit authoring/capture boundary and, where necessary, the pinned native export. Derive selected operations from native types/exports; retain binary, patch, version and schema provenance. Runtime consumers continue to use the sealed catalog. Do not add another repository `schemas/` authority, live schema fallback, generic parallel API client or second control plane. Unsupported capture remains an explicit gap or deferred feature.

Do not require complete HTTP/tool/WebSocket capture before removing the already captured plugin/skill wrappers. Capture becomes necessary when a selected migration depends on the missing contract.

## 5. Cognitive: complete counts and a bounded proposal

| Group | Methods | Current evidence / disposition |
|---|---:|---|
| Persona consultations | 567 | 81 personas × seven verbs. Shared native inference; persona/config improvements deferred under OD-122. |
| Execution catalog | 59 | 12 aliases backed by five executors. Existing dispatch uses identity-bearing `UnifiedExecution` D-Bus calls. Native shell/runtime overlap is a candidate, not proven language-operation equivalence. |
| Orchestration catalog | 18 | Six agents × three operations. Each child goes through canonical admission with the original caller. Native SOP/pipeline comparison may be deferred. |
| Memory operations | 7 | `memory_store/retrieve/query/recall/delete/list_namespaces/semantic_query`. Existing scoped Cozo owner, optional Qdrant semantics. OD-123 covers future native integration. |
| Code retrieval/indexing | 3 | `code_search`, `code_context`, `code_index`: Voyage/Qdrant and session-aware context. Generic native project/memory sections do not establish equivalent retrieval. |
| Compatibility agent facades | 6 | `rust_pro`, `python_pro`, `typescript_pro`, `sequential_thinking`, `context_manager`, `code_review_orchestrator`. |
| Workflow facades | 2 | `workflow_query/run`, sharing the local workstack owner. |
| Specialist/provider calls | 2 | `specialist` plus `gemini_query`; the latter has separate provider/research behavior. |
| Discovery/admission/policy | 6 | `get_health`, `list_tools`, `invoke_tool`, `schema_read`, `oscal_subids`, `toolsets`. |
| **Total** | **670** | **644 agent methods + 26 other methods.** |

The lesson's abbreviated list totaled 660. Persona consultations alone are **84.6%** of 670, not “over 85%.” These are generated declarations from [agent descriptors][E20], not 567 independently handwritten function implementations. The opportunity is reducing duplicate exposed contracts and local behavior that native facilities can own.

### What a persona migration actually needs to map

[specialist.rs][E9] shows that current consultations do more than append a static role: they validate the persona/verb, resolve the caller's route and mode, select a memory namespace, assemble dynamic persona pieces and scoped context, add role/knowledge, preserve the operation in the prompt, recheck admission, invoke provider-only completion and construct typed persona/source metadata.

The mounted Config's `AliasedAgentConfig` supports `identity`, `knowledge_bundles`, `skill_bundles`, `model_provider`, `risk_profile`, `runtime_profile`, `workspace`, `memory` and related fields. It has **no direct `system_prompt` field**. `IdentityConfig` supports OpenClaw/AIEOS documents and AIEOS inline/file sources. These establish native configuration mechanisms, not a completed translation of our prompt assembly.

**OD-122 proposal:** move static role/knowledge into appropriate native identity/bundle facilities where useful; map verbs, dynamic context and result metadata separately. Do not make exact reproduction of all 567 legacy method names a prerequisite for the first consolidation slice. Do not silently change provider-only consultation into tool-enabled agent execution.

**OD-123 proposal:** retain Cozo ownership and scope. The mounted `AgentMemoryConfig.backend` defaults to `sqlite`; `MemoryBackendKind` declares none/sqlite/postgres/qdrant/markdown/lucid, with no Cozo option. That is a concrete future integration gap. It is not authorization to add SQL/SQLite, switch stores, migrate data or silently disable memory. Other consolidation can proceed while this work stays on the wishlist.

Evidence: [mounted Config inside the native schema][E1], [specialist context/completion][E9], [execution dispatch][E21], [workflow admission][E22]. No agent configuration or memory backend was changed while preparing this brief.

## 6. Dependencies the implementing LLM must reconcile

| Dependency | Required treatment |
|---|---|
| Callers | Trace exact plugin/method references through bridge dispatch, UI, schema loaders, toolsets and generated outputs. Inspect the sibling UI's `src/chat/{door-chat-adapter,native-routing,control-plane-model,router-committed-route}.ts` and `src/grpc/door.ts`; do not assume one file handles every caller. Update the pinned UI input when the changed UI is part of a release. |
| Schema ownership | Make native operation shapes derive from the one native contract. Local policy/receipt integration must not independently reauthor native arguments/results. Never invent the target method name because the old owner used it. |
| State | Identify existing public/private state and child objects before changing owner paths. Preserve principal/session scope, unrelated children and authoritative Cozo data. Commit actual backend results to canonical SHM before notifications. Do not assume a global rename to `threetched` preserves state isolation. |
| Capability mapping | Build explicit old-method → canonical-operation → exact-capability mappings. Read/write distinctions, actor/session admission and current grants must survive. A hashed CLI capability is not automatically equivalent to an old typed read capability. No wildcard grants or direct policy rewrites to hide denials. |
| Receipts/errors | Distinguish execution failure, backend acceptance, state-publication failure, cancellation and recovery. A successful filesystem write or CLI exit alone is not proof of the full operation. |
| Mount selection | The host adapter currently hardcodes `threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills`. Update it consistently with actual catalog removals. Preserve our/upstream naming and separation. [Adapter source][E23]. |
| Generated/release inputs | Remove obsolete module/registry/dispatch references, regenerate affected derived views through existing mechanisms, prepare an isolated catalog, review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs and stage the matching binaries/config/UI. Do not hand-edit generated output as a second authority. |

For capability changes, preserving existing authorization is not permission to broaden it. Follow the repository's smallest-concrete-change procedure if a genuinely new grant is required. An operation denial is evidence to diagnose, not a reason to switch identities or transports.

## 7. Implementation sequence and completion evidence

This is a proposed sequence for the receiving agent. The owner asked this author to produce a prompt/document, not execute the application changes.

1. **Reconcile the shared work first.** Read current AGENTS/HANDOFF/SIGNALS and the mounted catalog. Two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source before the mapping hold, with related edits in `mod.rs`, `threetched.rs` and `mutation_engine.rs`; those removals remain unbuilt/unsealed/undeployed. Preserve unrelated work and finish this slice coherently rather than restarting it.
2. **Finish the directly captured wrapper slice.** Resolve plugin/skill command inputs, outputs, capabilities and callers against the 18 native commands. Reconcile mount selections and generated inputs. Record any feature deliberately retired/deferred instead of introducing replacement duplicate schemas.
3. **Migrate further proven overlaps in dependency order.** Select the next useful config/provider/cron/router subset. Add only the native capture needed by that subset; retain required local admission/state/receipt integration. Do not hold the first slice for full persona, memory or workflow parity.
4. **Build and prepare the release inputs.** Follow JEV's Cargo routing, one Cargo process, native `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, release `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`. Use the freshly built `opblob` for an isolated `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>` catalog with matching schema-shaping environment. Review removals and preserve recovery inputs. Golden consumes the already sealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.
5. **Hand off with exact status.** Report changed files, implemented/retired/deferred methods, build result, catalog delta, remaining blockers and next action. Live deployment, when explicitly included in the receiving task, uses `./activate-golden.sh` and snapshot send/receive; never hand-copy application binaries into the running host. Track host mount wiring separately from the application snapshot.

Evidence for a completed implementation slice includes resolved callers, one schema owner, exact catalog delta, successful required build and consistent release inputs. If deployed, add native activation/readiness receipts, mount/catalog agreement and resulting authoritative state where an admitted operation is available. Missing identity provisioning or an unavailable operation remains an explicit limitation.

**Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures remain owner-request-only.** The NotebookLM `cargo check --workspace` and persona-test gates are not automatic authority to run checks. Workspace scope and build execution follow the receiving prompt and current AGENTS. Report unrun tests as unrun. There is no claim of zero risk, guaranteed zero downtime or complete semantic parity.

Existing guard/storage holds and later subvolume pinning remain outside this scope. Future lungs MCP is neither a dependency of the first consolidation slice nor an interface to implement now.

## 8. What is ready to hand off

- **Grounded baseline:** mounted counts, real method names, native Config fields, current source ownership and the actual cron/generation/tool contract evidence.
- **First implementation slice:** finish the existing plugin/skill-wrapper removal and reconcile callers, mount selection, generated inputs and release catalog.
- **Subsequent slices:** migrate proven native overlap as needed contracts become available; track selected behavior and dependencies explicitly.
- **Deferred enhancements:** OD-122 native persona/configuration mapping; OD-123 Cozo-backed native memory integration. These do not block unrelated consolidation.
- **Current authoring status:** documentation and task-board changes only; no new application implementation, build, seal, deployment, grants, mounts or storage changes.

The implementation prompt is at the top of this file. The receiving LLM must reread present sources and shared ownership; this evidence is dated, not a substitute for current state.

## Evidence references

The original audit and fresh reads are complementary. Mounted declarations establish exposed contracts; code establishes implementation relationships; the NotebookLM artifact supplies synthesis and proposed structure. None alone proves a successful authenticated end-to-end operation.

content.text:
[deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/mount-3tchedfs#EC3C]
1:#!/bin/sh
2:### BEGIN INIT INFO
3:# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
4:# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
5:# Required-Stop:
6:# Default-Start:     S
7:# Default-Stop:
8:# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
9:### END INIT INFO
10:# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
11:# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
12:# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
13:set -eu
14:PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
15:export PATH
16:fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
17:case "${1:-}" in
18:    start)
19:        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
20:        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
21:        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
22:        ;;
23:    stop) exit 0 ;;
24:esac
25:[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
26:[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
27:    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
28:fs_name=$1
29:mount_path=$2
30:case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
31:    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
32:    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
33:    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
34:esac
35:upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
36:catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
37:options=$4
38:while [ -n "$options" ]; do
39:    option=${options%%,*}
40:    case "$option" in
41:        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
42:        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
43:    esac
44:    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
45:done
46:protected_file() {
47:    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
48:    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
49:}

#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
# Required-Stop:
# Default-Start:     S
# Default-Stop:
# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
### END INIT INFO
# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi
binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac
[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700
# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
# Required-Stop:
# Default-Start:     S
# Default-Stop:
# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
### END INIT INFO
# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi
binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac
[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700
# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

[reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.md#E8B3]
1:# Handwritten overlap with threetched — mounted-source map
2:
3:2026-10-18 · Codex `/root` with Luna `/root/schema_capture_build` and `/root/schema_capture_luna` · Task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121 · source HEAD `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a` plus shared uncommitted work.
4:
5:**Finding:** duplication extends beyond `tched_router`, `tched_plugins` and `tched_skills`. Confirmed wrappers also exist in LLM selection/generation, cron, native configuration, provider discovery and routing. Much of `cognitive` uses native threetched inference or covers domains native threetched already implements. The current capture is insufficient to establish complete operation equivalence: it captures CLI arguments and the native configuration schema, but omits native HTTP, WebSocket and tool contracts.
6:
7:**Owner direction:** use threetched as the authority for functionality it owns; collapse handwritten overlap into that surface. Moving the same declarations under `large_language_model` would preserve the duplicate authority and is superseded. Our filesystem/project code is `3tched`; the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime is `threetched`. Current access is filesystem I/O and the plugin is `cognitive`. Lungs becoming an MCP interface is a later step, after consolidation settles.
8:
9:This pass maps and reports only. No additional application edits, build, seal, deployment, mount changes or operation calls were made during the mapping pass. Two wrapper deletions made before the mapping instruction remain unbuilt and undeployed; see the final status below.
10:
11:## Evidence and coverage
12:
13:Primary reference: [`/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/threetched/schema.json`](/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/threetched/schema.json). Comparison set: the 70 schemas under `/run/mounts/3tchedFS/plugins/` and the four schemas under `/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/`. Source inspection disambiguates their implementations; it does not replace the mounted declarations as evidence of what is deployed.
14:
15:| Evidence | Observed value |
16:|---|---|
17:| Mounted catalog | 74 plugins, 1,388 method declarations |
18:| Our mount | 70 plugins, 1,180 methods |
19:| Upstream mount | `threetched` 147; `tched_router` 43; `tched_plugins` 6; `tched_skills` 12 |
20:| Native reference | 147 CLI operations and 83 top-level configuration sections |
21:| Cognitive | 670 methods; every name assigned to a functional group below |
22:| Binary / capture format | `threetched 0.8.4` / `threetched-cli/1` |
23:| Catalog generation | 74; before/after view inventories matched during enumeration |
24:| Catalog hash | `8a34d0da9517b137063314e07f5fa9a24fe3a3fe33920b1de2df941380041fd6` |
25:| threetched source schema hash | `5e27757d2c046632f9dcda0866fd58a6a0d38b14fc96ba19625f61166975149c` |
26:| Binary SHA-256 | `22e121f5eb1b66352138b714cc3d40d9eb977ed0c13bd6316f693a11a875a75e` |
27:| Native Config capture SHA-256 | `a98561f7b8c9f6a1be529557afc1bf123fee566958363cee211c998a5cb34cef` |
28:
29:The companion [machine-readable inventory](threetched-overlap-map-20261018.json) records every plugin and method name, declared capability, effect, idempotence, input/output field names, source path, assessment and reference targets. It includes the complete reference command list, configuration-section list and catalog object pins. It is an audit artifact, not a new runtime schema authority.
30:
31:Coverage means every mounted method was inventoried and screened; it does **not** mean 1,388 end-to-end semantic equivalence proofs. No authenticated invocation or cancellation was exercised. An ordinary read of mounted `tched_router/value.json` returned `Input/output error`; no alternate transport was used to obtain native tool state. Previously recorded human provisioning remains unresolved, so NotebookLM sync was not claimed or routed around.
32:
33:## Where the schema enters the blobs
34:
35:```mermaid
36:flowchart TD
37:    B[Verified threetched binary and manifest] --> C[Explicit capture: config schema and recursive CLI help]
38:    C --> T[threetched PluginSchema]
39:    H[Separately authored plugin declarations and wrappers] --> R[tched_router and other PluginSchemas]
40:    T --> S[opblob seals every registered PluginSchema]
41:    R --> S
42:    S --> K[Catalog: one blob per registered plugin ID]
43:    K --> G[Golden stages the presealed catalog]
44:    G --> D[Snapshot send/receive and activation]
45:    D --> F[Mounted filesystem projects sealed declarations and committed state]
46:```
47:
48:1. [`opblob.rs:688`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/bin/opblob.rs:688) explicitly calls `threetched::prepare_schema_capture` before sealing. Runtime startup consumes the catalog rather than discovering schemas again.
49:2. [`threetched.rs:54`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/threetched.rs:54) establishes one capture per explicit authoring process; its capture path verifies the selected binary, manifest, version and digests.
50:3. [`threetched-surface.rs:180`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/threetched-fs/src/threetched-surface.rs:180) captures `config schema`, recursive `--help`, and `--version`, then checks that the binary did not change. `schema_from_capture` turns that into the `threetched` PluginSchema, including per-command capabilities.
51:4. The sealer obtains each registered plugin's schema. [`op-blob/src/lib.rs:72`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/lib.rs:72) canonicalizes and seals the **full** PluginSchema in `SCHEMA_JSON`; reflection/manifest views derive from that same value.
52:5. [`catalog.rs:153`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/catalog.rs:153) writes `<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` and updates the catalog. A full reseal removes IDs absent from the build via `retain_plugins`.
53:6. Golden preparation validates/stages an already sealed catalog. Deployment transports the snapshot; FUSE projects its blobs. FUSE does not invent or reseal an upstream schema when a file is read.
54:
55:**The duplicate authority is introduced before sealing.** Separate handwritten plugin registrations become separate blobs even when one native binary owns their behavior. A single catalog does not remove that duplication. Capturing native Config once also does not automatically derive the handwritten HTTP, generation or tool declarations from it.
56:
57:## Confirmed wrappers and shared native backends
58:
59:“Confirmed” below means the wrapper/backend relationship is supported by source. It does not assert that replacing a typed method with a CLI command preserves its complete result, identity and receipt contract.
60:
61:| Current surface | Mounted/native reference | Finding and obligations |
62:|---|---|---|
63:| `tched_plugins` — all 6 | `plugin.install/list/migrate/info/remove/search` | Direct duplicated native plugin-command surface. Current names: `install_plugin`, `list_plugins`, `migrate_plugins`, `plugin_info`, `remove_plugin`, `search_plugins`. |
64:| `tched_skills` — all 12 | `skills.add/audit/edit/install/list/remove/test`; `skills.bundle.add/list/remove/rename/show` | Direct duplicated native skill-command surface. Bundle and skill methods map one-for-one by action. |
65:| `large_language_model` — all 8 | Router facade over native providers/models/config/generation | `list_providers→ListProviders`; `get_provider/get_config→GetState`; `set_provider→SetProvider`; `generate→Chat`; `stream_generate→start_generation`; `list_models→ListModels`; `update_config→SetSelection`. Has no independent state owner. Native completion and selection must remain authoritative when callers move. |
66:| `cron` — all 9 use the native store | `cron.add/list/update/resume/pause/remove`; native HTTP cron API | `create_job→cron.add` (also native add-at/add-every/once variants); `list_jobs/get_job→cron.list`; update/enable/disable/delete→update/resume/pause/remove. `get_history` and `run_job` use native HTTP routes omitted from the CLI capture. Preserve typed jobs, scoped access, publication diagnostics, indeterminate-outcome receipts and SHM readback. |
67:| `mcp` — 2 of 3 | Native `/mcp` Config section; `config.get/patch` | `get_config→GetMcpConfig`; `configure_server→PatchConfig`, restricted to server descendants. `configure_tool_groups` is local bridge projection policy and needs a separate relevance decision for the current filesystem interface. Its existence does not authorize an MCP implementation now. |
68:| `gemma_brain.route` — 1 of 17 | `model_routes`; native routing | Direct `ResolveRoute` facade. Exact native resolver result contract is not captured. Other 16 methods include UI, classification and tag behavior; native inference alone does not establish equivalence for them. |
69:| `model_registry.native_list_providers` — 1 of 6 | `providers`, `providers.list`, `/providers` | Uses native provider inventory with additional protected-agent-profile filtering. The other five methods mix provider metadata, credentials and local model profiles; see candidate mapping. |
70:| Cognitive personas + `specialist` — 568 | `agent`, `agents.*`; `/agents`, `/delegate`, profiles/bundles | Demonstrated shared threetched completion backend. Local prompt/persona/context assembly is additional behavior to map; it does not justify 568 independently authored schema operations. |
71:
72:Implementation evidence: [LLM facade](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/large_language_model_methods.rs:44), [cron gateway](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/cron_gateway.rs:123), [MCP config facade](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/mcp_methods.rs:62), [model registry dispatcher](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/model_registry_dispatch.rs:1021), [persona completion](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/specialist.rs:383).
73:
74:## All 43 router methods
75:
76:| Group | Methods | Reference and unresolved contract |
77:|---|---|---|
78:| Config/schema — 15 | `GetConfig`, `GetConfigSchema`, `GetMcpConfig`, `PatchConfig`; `config_get`, `config_init`, `config_list`, `config_migrate`, `config_patch`, `config_set`; `get`, `init`, `list`, `patch`, `set` | Same native Config domain as `config.*`. Native HTTP property/list/patch/init/migrate response and error types exist in pinned source but are absent from the current CLI capture. Masked secrets, revision/coherent observation and alias behavior require explicit reconciliation. |
79:| Inventory/projection — 9 | `GetState`, `GetProviderCatalog`, `GetModelRoutes`, `GetRouter`, `GetStructuredOutput`, `GetTools`, `ListModels`, `ListProviders`, `ListUiSurfaces` | Providers/models/config sections overlap. `GetTools` reads native `/api/tools` but drops native `param_domains`; no tool declarations are captured as native methods. UI/structured-output and complete committed-state projections need field-level comparison. |
80:| Selection/routing/bindings — 12 | `SetModel`, `SetProvider`, `SetSelection`, `SetCozoRetrievalModel`, `SetObfuscationModel`, `SetOvsRoutingModel`, `SetQdrantRetrievalModel`, `SetVectorizationModel`, `ResolveRoute`, `apply_catalog_model_binding`, `resolve_catalog_model_binding`, `get_own_agent_route` | Native `/providers`, `/agents`, `/model_routes`, `/embedding_routes`, `models.set` and config mutation cover the domain. Local role names, catalog-model bindings, caller-specific routes and atomic selection/admission are obligations to map, not grounds for retaining a second schema owner. |
81:| Generation — 7 | `Chat`, `start_generation`, `cancel_generation`, `get_generation_job`, `get_generation_jobs`, `delete_generation_job`, `recover_generation_jobs` | Native `agent` and patched stateless `/ws/chat` supply inference. OP-DBUS job CRUD, private committed SHM state, recovery and cancellation semantics are not shown equivalent by the current native capture. Capture native frames/errors/cancellation first, then separate true local job bookkeeping from duplicated generation declarations. |
82:
83:Source: [router declarations](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/tched_router.rs:1863), [native tools adapter](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/tched_router_legacy_dispatch.rs:89), [pinned generation patch](/srv/git/odbus-verified/vendor/tched-router/patches/0002-stateless-provider-generation.patch).
84:
85:Known affected callers include LLM/MCP facades, specialist/agent dispatch, generation admission and publisher, model registry, cron/config paths, schema loader/server defaults, UI workspace/schema consumers, op-web state/SSE/routes, and the sibling UI's `src/chat/{door-chat-adapter,native-routing,control-plane-model,router-committed-route}.ts`. These dependencies identify migration work; they do not justify preserving another upstream schema authority. The shipped pinned UI archive must move with its source when those callers change.
86:
87:## All 670 cognitive methods
88:
89:Names and counts come from the mounted `cognitive` schema. The machine inventory assigns each method to one group.
90:
91:| Group | Count | Native overlap / additional behavior |
92:|---|---:|---|
93:| Persona consultations | 567 | 81 personas × `advise/analyze/consult/explain/help/recommend/review`. Native completion is shared; local persona prompts and scoped context must be mapped to native agents/profiles. |
94:| Execution catalog | 59 | 12 exposed aliases backed by five executors: Rust 12, Python 12, JavaScript/TypeScript 18, Go 15, shell 2. Native `/shell_tool`, runtime and agent profiles overlap functionally. Current implementation uses `UnifiedExecution` D-Bus `ExecuteCatalog`; identity/project restrictions and language wrappers must be compared with native tool contracts. |
95:| Orchestration catalog | 18 | Six agents × `list_steps/run_workflow/validate`: code-review-orchestrator, context-manager, dx-optimizer, memory, sequential-thinking, tdd-orchestrator. Native pipeline/delegate/SOP domains overlap. Preserve child-by-child admission, cancellation and committed results. |
96:| Memory | 7 | `memory_store/retrieve/query/recall/delete/list_namespaces/semantic_query`. Native `memory.get/list/clear`, `/memory` and embedding config overlap. Current namespace selection is server-bound to caller mode/session; `memory_recall` already aliases query internally. Exact native put/delete/query tool shapes are missing. |
97:| Code retrieval/indexing | 3 | `code_search`, `code_context`, `code_index`. Native `/project_intel`, `/memory`, `/web_search` are related; symbol filtering, Voyage collections and session context equivalence is unproven. |
98:| Compatibility agent facades | 6 | `rust_pro`, `python_pro`, `typescript_pro`, `sequential_thinking`, `context_manager`, `code_review_orchestrator` normalize into catalog methods above. Three are execution aliases and three orchestration aliases. |
99:| Workflow facades | 2 | `workflow_query/run` use the same local workstack owner as `workflows.query_workflows/start_workflow`; native SOP/pipeline equivalence still needs mapping. |
100:| Specialist/provider calls | 2 | `specialist` shares native completion. `gemini_query` is a separate Gemini HTTPS/research implementation: likely provider/search overlap, but grounded citations/deep-research result compatibility is not captured. |
101:| Discovery/admission/policy | 6 | `get_health`, `list_tools`, `invoke_tool`, `schema_read`, `oscal_subids`, `toolsets`. Current bridge/catalog policy and dispatch; native tool discovery is related, but OP-DBUS identity/capability/schema semantics are not proven replaceable. |
102:| **Total** | **670** | **644 agent methods + 26 core/facade methods.** |
103:
104:Source: [cognitive registration](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/cognitive_agents.rs:331), [agent descriptors](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-agents/src/agent_catalog.rs:45), [registered implementations](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-cognitive/src/agent_tools.rs:16), [execution dispatch](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/agent_catalog_dispatch.rs:136), [workflow dispatch](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/agent_workflow.rs:31), [code tools](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-cognitive/src/code_tools.rs:1).
105:
106:There is no standalone cognitive file-read/write or browser method among these 670 names. `agent_search_specialist_*` is persona consultation; `agent_memory_*` is orchestration. Native `/browser`, `/browser_delegate`, `/file_download`, `/file_upload`, `/web_fetch` do not establish a matching cognitive method merely because the domain sounds similar.
107:
108:## Native capture gaps that block a complete collapse map
109:
110:| Missing in mounted capture | Evidence in pinned native implementation | Needed comparison |
111:|---|---|---|
112:| Typed config HTTP operations | `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_config.rs`: property/list/patch/init/migrate types; `openapi.rs::build_spec` exposes a config/version OpenAPI subset | Native request/result/error types, masked fields, revisions and authorization. Config JSON alone is not the method contract. |
113:| Native tool catalog | Existing adapter reads `/api/tools`: name, description, parameters, optional output, plus upstream `param_domains` discarded by adapter | Shell, memory, browser, file, search and delegate inputs/results; capability and state ownership. No successful current mounted tool-state read was available. |
114:| WebSocket generation | Pinned patch implements `tched_router.generation.v1`, connect/prompt and session_start/connected/chunk/done/error frames | SID1 forwarding, provider/model selection, usage, cancellation, failure and disconnect semantics; distinguish native inference from local job receipts. |
115:| Native cron HTTP | Existing cron gateway uses `/api/cron`, per-job `/runs`, and `/run` | Typed job/history/run results and errors, scoped state, non-CLI operations. |

# Handwritten overlap with threetched — mounted-source map

2026-10-18 · Codex `/root` with Luna `/root/schema_capture_build` and `/root/schema_capture_luna` · Task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121 · source HEAD `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a` plus shared uncommitted work.

**Finding:** duplication extends beyond `tched_router`, `tched_plugins` and `tched_skills`. Confirmed wrappers also exist in LLM selection/generation, cron, native configuration, provider discovery and routing. Much of `cognitive` uses native threetched inference or covers domains native threetched already implements. The current capture is insufficient to establish complete operation equivalence: it captures CLI arguments and the native configuration schema, but omits native HTTP, WebSocket and tool contracts.

**Owner direction:** use threetched as the authority for functionality it owns; collapse handwritten overlap into that surface. Moving the same declarations under `large_language_model` would preserve the duplicate authority and is superseded. Our filesystem/project code is `3tched`; the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime is `threetched`. Current access is filesystem I/O and the plugin is `cognitive`. Lungs becoming an MCP interface is a later step, after consolidation settles.

This pass maps and reports only. No additional application edits, build, seal, deployment, mount changes or operation calls were made during the mapping pass. Two wrapper deletions made before the mapping instruction remain unbuilt and undeployed; see the final status below.

## Evidence and coverage

Primary reference: [`/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/threetched/schema.json`](/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/threetched/schema.json). Comparison set: the 70 schemas under `/run/mounts/3tchedFS/plugins/` and the four schemas under `/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/`. Source inspection disambiguates their implementations; it does not replace the mounted declarations as evidence of what is deployed.

| Our mount | 70 plugins, 1,180 methods |
