## Where the schema enters the blobs

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[Verified threetched binary and manifest] --> C[Explicit capture: config schema and recursive CLI help]
    C --> T[threetched PluginSchema]
    H[Separately authored plugin declarations and wrappers] --> R[tched_router and other PluginSchemas]
    T --> S[opblob seals every registered PluginSchema]
    R --> S
    S --> K[Catalog: one blob per registered plugin ID]
    K --> G[Golden stages the presealed catalog]
    G --> D[Snapshot send/receive and activation]
    D --> F[Mounted filesystem projects sealed declarations and committed state]
```

1. [`opblob.rs:688`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/bin/opblob.rs:688) explicitly calls `threetched::prepare_schema_capture` before sealing. Runtime startup consumes the catalog rather than discovering schemas again.
2. [`threetched.rs:54`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/threetched.rs:54) establishes one capture per explicit authoring process; its capture path verifies the selected binary, manifest, version and digests.
3. [`threetched-surface.rs:180`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/threetched-fs/src/threetched-surface.rs:180) captures `config schema`, recursive `--help`, and `--version`, then checks that the binary did not change. `schema_from_capture` turns that into the `threetched` PluginSchema, including per-command capabilities.
4. The sealer obtains each registered plugin's schema. [`op-blob/src/lib.rs:72`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/lib.rs:72) canonicalizes and seals the **full** PluginSchema in `SCHEMA_JSON`; reflection/manifest views derive from that same value.
5. [`catalog.rs:153`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/catalog.rs:153) writes `<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` and updates the catalog. A full reseal removes IDs absent from the build via `retain_plugins`.
6. Golden preparation validates/stages an already sealed catalog. Deployment transports the snapshot; FUSE projects its blobs. FUSE does not invent or reseal an upstream schema when a file is read.

**The duplicate authority is introduced before sealing.** Separate handwritten plugin registrations become separate blobs even when one native binary owns their behavior. # Handwritten overlap with threetched — mounted-source map

2026-10-18 · Codex `/root` with Luna `/root/schema_capture_build` and `/root/schema_capture_luna` · Task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121 · source HEAD `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a` plus shared uncommitted work.

**Finding:** duplication extends beyond `tched_router`, `tched_plugins` and `tched_skills`. Confirmed wrappers also exist in LLM selection/generation, cron, native configuration, provider discovery and routing. Much of `cognitive` uses native threetched inference or covers domains native threetched already implements. The current capture is insufficient to establish complete operation equivalence: it captures CLI arguments and the native configuration schema, but omits native HTTP, WebSocket and tool contracts.

**Owner direction:** use threetched as the authority for functionality it owns; collapse handwritten overlap into that surface. Moving the same declarations under `large_language_model` would preserve the duplicate authority and is superseded. Our filesystem/project code is `3tched`; the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime is `threetched`. Current access is filesystem I/O and the plugin is `cognitive`. Lungs becoming an MCP interface is a later step, after consolidation settles.

This pass maps and reports only. No additional application edits, build, seal, deployment, mount changes or operation calls were made during the mapping pass. Two wrapper deletions made before the mapping instruction remain unbuilt and undeployed; see the final status below.

## Evidence and coverage

Primary reference: [`/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/threetched/schema.json`](/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/threetched/schema.json). Comparison set: the 70 schemas under `/run/mounts/3tchedFS/plugins/` and the four schemas under `/run/mounts/threetched/plugins/`. Source inspection disambiguates their implementations; it does not replace the mounted declarations as evidence of what is deployed.

| Evidence | Observed value |
|---|---|
| Mounted catalog | 74 plugins, 1,388 method declarations |
| Our mount | 70 plugins, 1,180 methods |
| Upstream mount | `threetched` 147; `tched_router` 43; `tched_plugins` 6; `tched_skills` 12 |
| Native reference | 147 CLI operations and 83 top-level configuration sections |
| Cognitive | 670 methods; every name assigned to a functional group below |
| Binary / capture format | `threetched 0.8.4` / `threetched-cli/1` |

The companion [machine-readable inventory](threetched-overlap-map-20261018.json) records every plugin and method name, declared capability, effect, idempotence, input/output field names, source path, assessment and reference targets. It includes the complete reference command list, configuration-section list and catalog object pins. It is an audit artifact, not a new runtime schema authority.

Coverage means every mounted method was inventoried and screened; it does **not** mean 1,388 end-to-end semantic equivalence proofs. No authenticated invocation or cancellation was exercised. An ordinary read of mounted `tched_router/value.json` returned `Input/output error`; no alternate transport was used to obtain native tool state. Previously recorded human provisioning remains unresolved, so NotebookLM sync was not claimed or routed around.

## Where the schema enters the blobs

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    B[Verified threetched binary and manifest] --> C[Explicit capture: config schema and recursive CLI help]
    C --> T[threetched PluginSchema]
    H[Separately authored plugin declarations and wrappers] --> R[tched_router and other PluginSchemas]
    T --> S[opblob seals every registered PluginSchema]
    R --> S
    S --> K[Catalog: one blob per registered plugin ID]
    K --> G[Golden stages the presealed catalog]
    G --> D[Snapshot send/receive and activation]
    D --> F[Mounted filesystem projects sealed declarations and committed state]
```

1. [`opblob.rs:688`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/bin/opblob.rs:688) explicitly calls `threetched::prepare_schema_capture` before sealing. Runtime startup consumes the catalog rather than discovering schemas again.
2. [`threetched.rs:54`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/threetched.rs:54) establishes one capture per explicit authoring process; its capture path verifies the selected binary, manifest, version and digests.
3. [`threetched-surface.rs:180`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/threetched-fs/src/threetched-surface.rs:180) captures `config schema`, recursive `--help`, and `--version`, then checks that the binary did not change. `schema_from_capture` turns that into the `threetched` PluginSchema, including per-command capabilities.
4. The sealer obtains each registered plugin's schema. [`op-blob/src/lib.rs:72`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/lib.rs:72) canonicalizes and seals the **full** PluginSchema in `SCHEMA_JSON`; reflection/manifest views derive from that same value.
5. [`catalog.rs:153`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/crates/op-blob/src/catalog.rs:153) writes `<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` and updates the catalog. A full reseal removes IDs absent from the build via `retain_plugins`.
6. Golden preparation validates/stages an already sealed catalog. Deployment transports the snapshot; FUSE projects its blobs. FUSE does not invent or reseal an upstream schema when a file is read.

**The duplicate authority is introduced before sealing.** Separate handwritten plugin registrations become separate blobs even when one native binary owns their behavior. A single catalog does not remove that duplication. Capturing native Config once also does not automatically derive the handwritten HTTP, generation or tool declarations from it.

There is no standalone cognitive file-read/write or browser method among these 670 names. `agent_search_specialist_*` is persona consultation; `agent_memory_*` is orchestration. Native `/browser`, `/browser_delegate`, `/file_download`, `/file_upload`, `/web_fetch` do not establish a matching cognitive method merely because the domain sounds similar.

## Native capture gaps that block a complete collapse map

| Missing in mounted capture | Evidence in pinned native implementation | Needed comparison |
|---|---|---|
| Typed config HTTP operations | `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/api_config.rs`: property/list/patch/init/migrate types; `openapi.rs::build_spec` exposes a config/version OpenAPI subset | Native request/result/error types, masked fields, revisions and authorization. Config JSON alone is not the method contract. |
| Native tool catalog | Existing adapter reads `/api/tools`: name, description, parameters, optional output, plus upstream `param_domains` discarded by adapter | Shell, memory, browser, file, search and delegate inputs/results; capability and state ownership. No successful current mounted tool-state read was available. |
| WebSocket generation | Pinned patch implements `tched_router.generation.v1`, connect/prompt and session_start/connected/chunk/done/error frames | SID1 forwarding, provider/model selection, usage, cancellation, failure and disconnect semantics; distinguish native inference from local job receipts. |
| Native cron HTTP | Existing cron gateway uses `/api/cron`, per-job `/runs`, and `/run` | Typed job/history/run results and errors, scoped state, non-CLI operations. |
| Other gateway facilities | Pinned native gateway declares chat, SOP-run and canvas WebSockets, among other APIs | Native availability is demonstrated in source; complete exported operation contracts and equivalence remain uncaptured. |

Pinned input: [`vendor/tched-router/source.pin`](/srv/git/odbus-verified/vendor/tched-router/source.pin), source archive `vendor/tched-router/source.tar.gz`, upstream v0.8.4 commit `a56c345d51dd8ab562e9351e0d4ab83f6a741db9`, plus checked-in patches. No upstream HTTP/WS call was made in this audit.

The present 147 CLI methods all declare `mutation`, `idempotent=false`, a per-command hashed capability, and `{stdout, stderr, exit}` output. This is useful command discovery, but is materially weaker than typed domain results and errors. It cannot by itself justify replacing read methods, narrowing grants or preserving cancellation/state publication. Native capture needs to supply those missing contracts at the existing authoring boundary, with provenance, without a new parallel `schemas/` authority.

details.oldText:
#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
# Required-Stop:
# Default-Start:     S
# Default-Stop:
# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
### END INIT INFO
# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi
binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac
[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700
# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
# Required-Stop:
# Default-Start:     S
# Default-Stop:
# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
### END INIT INFO
# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi

store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'

    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac

ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700

    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &

        exit 0
    fi

    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done

#!/bin/sh
### BEGIN INIT INFO
# Provides:          op-3tchedfs-mount
# Required-Start:    op-release-activate
# Required-Stop:
# Default-Start:     S
# Default-Stop:
# Short-Description: Mount separate OP-DBUS and threetched views from fstab
### END INIT INFO
# The release stages this adapter in /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers.
# /usr/sbin/mount.fuse.3tchedFS and rcS/S13op-3tchedfs-mount link there.
# The fstab noauto entry is mounted explicitly after S12op-release-activate.
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
export PATH
fail() { printf 'mount-3tchedfs: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
case "${1:-}" in
    start)
        [ "$#" = 1 ] || exit 2
        mount /run/mounts/3tchedFS
        exec mount /run/mounts/threetched
        ;;
    stop) exit 0 ;;
esac
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host mount owner must be root'
[ "$#" = 4 ] && [ "$3" = -o ] ||
    fail 'expected the declared 3tchedFS fstab entry'
fs_name=$1
mount_path=$2
case "$fs_name:$mount_path" in
    3tchedFS:/run/mounts/3tchedFS) selection=--exclude-plugin ;;
    threetched:/run/mounts/threetched) selection=--include-plugin ;;
    *) fail 'unexpected mount source or target' ;;
esac
upstream_plugins=threetched,tched_router,tched_plugins,tched_skills
catalog=/usr/share/op-dbus/plugin-blobs
options=$4
while [ -n "$options" ]; do
    option=${options%%,*}
    case "$option" in
        rw|noauto|nosuid|nodev|noexec|noatime|defaults) ;;
        *) fail "unsupported mount option: $option" ;;
    esac
    case "$options" in *,*) options=${options#*,} ;; *) options= ;; esac
done
protected_file() {
    [ -f "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || return 1
    case "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" in 0:0:400|0:0:600) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
session_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-session
owner_file=/etc/op-dbus/human-lungs-call-owner-uid
protected_file "$session_file" && protected_file "$owner_file" || fail 'unsafe or absent host identity selection'
session=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$session_file")
printf '%s\n' "$session" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' || fail 'invalid session'
owner_uid=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$owner_file")
case "$owner_uid" in ''|*[!0-9]*) fail 'invalid local caller UID' ;; esac
[ "$owner_uid" = "$(id -u jeremy)" ] || fail 'local operator UID changed'
ensure_dir() {
    if [ ! -e "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ]; then mkdir -m "$2" "$1"; fi
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] && [ "$(stat -c '%u:%g:%a' "$1")" = "0:0:$2" ] ||
        fail "unsafe directory: $1"
}
ensure_dir /run/opdbus 755
ensure_dir /run/opdbus/host-fuse 700
runtime=/run/opdbus/host-fuse/$fs_name
ensure_dir "$runtime" 700
umask 077
exec 9>"$runtime/adapter.lock"
flock -w 15 9 || fail 'another mount invocation is active'
mounted_kind() { findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o FSTYPE; }
ready() {
    [ "$(mounted_kind)" = fuse.3tchedFS ] || return 1
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$mount_path" -o SOURCE)" = "$fs_name" ] || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg session "$session" --argjson uid "$owner_uid" '
        .mount_identity.kind == "host_session" and
        .mount_identity.session == $session and
        .local_call_owner_uid == $uid and .workspace_id == null
    ' "$mount_path/.3tchedfs.json" >/dev/null || return 1
    timeout 3 jq -e --arg name "$fs_name" --arg upstream "$upstream_plugins" \
        --slurpfile catalog "$catalog/.manifest.json" '
        ($upstream | split(",") | sort) as $upstream |
        (.objects | keys | sort) as $actual |
        (.source_catalog_hash == $catalog[0].catalog_hash and
         .source_catalog_generation == $catalog[0].generation) and
        (if $name == "threetched" then $actual == $upstream
        else (.objects | has("tched_fs")) and
            ($actual == (($catalog[0].plugins | keys | sort) - $upstream))
        end)
    ' "$mount_path/view.json" >/dev/null
}
if [ -n "$(mounted_kind)" ]; then
    ready || fail 'existing mount differs from the declared identity or release view'
    date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
    exit 0
fi
binary=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs
store=/dev/shm/3tchedfs-$fs_name
[ -x "$binary" ] && [ -f "$catalog/.manifest.json" ] || fail 'committed release is unavailable'
case "$(findmnt -rn -M /usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin -o SOURCE)" in
    opdbus-release:*) ;; *) fail 'application binary target is not an active release' ;;
esac
[ -c /dev/fuse ] || fail 'missing /dev/fuse'
ensure_dir /run/mounts 755
ensure_dir "$mount_path" 755
[ -z "$(find "$mount_path" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -print -quit)" ] || fail 'mountpoint is not empty'
ensure_dir "$store" 700
# Mount sealed declarations before bridge startup. Operations still require
# the existing session and grants; no identity/state is manufactured here.
"$binary" --store "$store" capture --schema-only --catalog "$catalog" --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    "$selection" "$upstream_plugins" >"$runtime/capture.json"
nohup setsid "$binary" --store "$store" mount \
    --fs-name "$fs_name" \
    --catalog /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs --state /dev/shm/opdbus/state \
    --allow-other --auto-unmount --call-owner-uid "$owner_uid" \
    --lungs-socket /run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock --lungs-session "$session" \
    "$mount_path" >"$runtime/daemon.log" 2>&1 </dev/null 9>&- &
daemon_pid=$!
printf '%s\n' "$daemon_pid" >"$runtime/daemon.pid"
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt 100 ]; do
    if ready; then
        date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ >"$runtime/fstab-ready-at"
        exit 0
    fi
    kill -0 "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    sleep 0.1
done
kill "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
wait "$daemon_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
fail "mount did not become ready; see $runtime/daemon.log"

**Ghostbridge Live!** is the name of the whole effort: taking the architecture from
deployed-but-dark to *running live* — registration → Qdrant/Gemma → accountability loop →
routing → chatbot → demo. This board is the single source of truth for all of it.
Replaces scattered TODO fragments across `.zenflow/tasks/`, `.kiro/specs/`, and notebook snapshots.

coverage count does not mean every declared surface requires a server backend;
determine server/decoy applicability or retirement before implementing a handler.

- **Priority buckets:** Critical/Urgent → Current → Next → Future → When I Have Staff.

- **Dispatch:** tell Claude *"dispatch <ID> to <agent>"* — it spawns that agent with the task

# 👻 GHOSTBRIDGE LIVE! — Working Wishlist / Task Board

**Ghostbridge Live!** is the name of the whole effort: taking the architecture from
deployed-but-dark to *running live* — registration → Qdrant/Gemma → accountability loop →
routing → chatbot → demo. This board is the single source of truth for all of it.
Replaces scattered TODO fragments across `.zenflow/tasks/`, `.kiro/specs/`, and notebook snapshots.

**Owner topology correction (2026-09-13):** WireGuard terminates at the decoy;
there is no WireGuard on this server. Identity is transported by WARP. Apply
this correction when interpreting older task descriptions. OD-55's source
coverage count does not mean every declared surface requires a server backend;
determine server/decoy applicability or retirement before implementing a handler.

## How to use this board

- **Priority buckets:** Critical/Urgent → Current → Next → Future → When I Have Staff.
- **Status:** `TODO` · `WIP` · `BLOCKED` · `DONE`.
- **Agent:** who's assigned — an `op-agents` role (`devops`, `policy_enforcer`, `schema_as_code`)
  or a Claude Code subagent (`Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`, `claude`).
- **Dispatch:** tell Claude *"dispatch <ID> to <agent>"* — it spawns that agent with the task
  context and updates Status here when done.
- **Add work:** append a row under the right bucket with a fresh `OD-##` id.

# 👻 GHOSTBRIDGE LIVE! — Working Wishlist / Task Board

**Ghostbridge Live!** is the name of the whole effort: taking the architecture from
deployed-but-dark to *running live* — registration → Qdrant/Gemma → accountability loop →
routing → chatbot → demo. This board is the single source of truth for all of it.
Replaces scattered TODO fragments across `.zenflow/tasks/`, `.kiro/specs/`, and notebook snapshots.

**Owner topology correction (2026-09-13):** WireGuard terminates at the decoy;
there is no WireGuard on this server. Identity is transported by WARP. Apply
this correction when interpreting older task descriptions. OD-55's source
coverage count does not mean every declared surface requires a server backend;
determine server/decoy applicability or retirement before implementing a handler.

## How to use this board

- **Priority buckets:** Critical/Urgent → Current → Next → Future → When I Have Staff.
- **Status:** `TODO` · `WIP` · `BLOCKED` · `DONE`.
- **Agent:** who's assigned — an `op-agents` role (`devops`, `policy_enforcer`, `schema_as_code`)
  or a Claude Code subagent (`Explore`, `Plan`, `general-purpose`, `claude`).
- **Dispatch:** tell Claude *"dispatch <ID> to <agent>"* — it spawns that agent with the task
  context and updates Status here when done.
- **Add work:** append a row under the right bucket with a fresh `OD-##` id.

[reports/threetched-consolidation-handoff-20261018.md#A5E9]
1:# Implementation prompt
2:
3:Implement threetched consolidation in `/srv/git/odbus-verified`, using the grounded implementation brief included below this prompt in this same file. Read that brief in full before editing.
4:
5:Read `AGENTS.md` and all its mandatory skill preloads first, then current `HANDOFF.md`, relevant `SIGNALS.md`, `WISHLIST.md`, the brief, and:
6:
7:- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.md`
8:- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.txt` — JSON method inventory with a sharing-friendly extension.
9:
10:The original NotebookLM report is a synthesis of supplied sources, not live verification. The grounded brief supersedes its unsupported endpoint names, equivalence claims and automatic test gates. Verify present code and mounted declarations before relying on dated counts or source locations.
11:
12:## Objective
13:
14:Collapse handwritten operations already owned by the native threetched runtime into its one native-derived plugin schema. Keep our code under the 3tched distinction and the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime under threetched. Do not relocate duplicate declarations into `large_language_model`, another plugin, a separate schema directory or a new transport shim.
15:
16:Deliver working implementation and required build/catalog preparation, not another plan. Make the largest coherent, evidence-backed consolidation you can complete without speculative feature expansion. Begin with the direct plugin/skill wrappers, then continue into other established overlaps in dependency order. Explicitly record remaining work and blockers; do not describe a partial slice as complete consolidation.
17:
18:Full feature parity is not required. Missing persona/configuration features are **OD-122**, and native memory integration is **OD-123**. Those are wishlist work, not prerequisites for unrelated consolidation. Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority. Introduce no SQL/SQLite backend, automatic data migration or silent memory substitution. Existing unrelated migration debt is not this task.
19:
20:Current access is filesystem I/O, and the current name is **cognitive**. Lungs becomes an MCP interface after consolidation settles; do not implement that future interface here.
21:
22:## Implementation requirements
23:
24:1. Claim ownership in HANDOFF before editing. Preserve shared changes. The two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source, with associated module/dispatch/hash-helper edits, but that removal was not built, sealed or deployed. Reconcile and finish it; do not reset or blindly repeat it.
25:
26:2. Begin with the mounted namespaces `/run/mounts/threetched` and `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`. Discover supported contracts there. Use pinned native source/export code to diagnose missing capture through the repository's supported maintenance/authoring path. Preserve caller identity and capability checks; do not bypass an absent or denied operation with another identity or transport.
27:
28:3. Complete the direct-wrapper slice: map all six `tched_plugins` and twelve `tched_skills` operations to the already captured native commands; reconcile arguments/results, callers, exact capabilities, registry/module/dispatch references, generated artifacts and mount selection. The mount adapter currently lists all four upstream IDs. Catalog removal and the adapter must agree.
29:
30:4. For additional config/provider/cron/router/LLM/cognitive overlap, assign every affected method a concrete disposition: migrate now, retain a genuine local integration responsibility, defer, or retire. Existing caller dependencies identify migration work; they do not justify a second native schema authority. Reconcile callers for removed or deferred behavior and expose truthful unsupported/unavailable outcomes instead of fake success.
31:
32:5. Add only the native capture required for the selected operations. Extend the existing verified native export/capture and explicit `opblob` authoring boundary. Runtime continues to consume sealed blobs. Do not invent `threetched.Chat`, HTTP endpoints, WebSocket frames or native memory support. The brief contains the observed real names and source references. Missing capture does not mean a feature is absent, and a configuration section is not an HTTP endpoint.
33:
34:6. Keep identity admission, private state partitions, exact grants, committed SHM publication, receipt/error semantics and cancellation outcomes intact for delivered operations. Do not globally rename state ownership or rewrite grants without tracing the affected contracts. Native stream disconnect does not prove a provider request was undone. No wildcard grants, new identity, blanket capability expansion or security-policy weakening.
35:
36:7. Update demonstrated consumers across the bridge, generated surfaces, toolsets, the sibling `/srv/git/3tched.com` UI and its pinned release input where affected. A compatibility name may temporarily resolve to the canonical declaration and admission path; it must not establish a separately authored schema. Do not retain wrappers indefinitely merely to avoid migrating callers.
37:
38:## Build, catalog and deployment boundary
39:
40:This prompt requests a native GNU release workspace build for the resulting cross-crate change:
41:
42:```sh
43:CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
44:```
45:
46:Use the repository's existing JEV execution routing without model overrides. Run one Cargo process at a time; respect an existing build. Keep the primary agent available for source review and communication. Every delegated agent must perform its own mandatory preload and share task/file ownership.
47:
48:Use the freshly built `target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/opblob` to prepare a **new isolated catalog** through `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>`, with the service's current schema-shaping environment. Review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs, retain recoverable inputs and ensure matching binaries, generated views, configuration and any affected pinned UI input. Golden consumes the presealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.
49:
50:The default deliverable for this prompt is implemented source, required build results, isolated release inputs and a precise deployment handoff. If the owner separately includes live activation in the receiving task, use only the canonical `./activate-golden.sh` snapshot/send-receive path and its receipts. Never hand-copy application binaries into the live installation. Keep host mount wiring and rollback implications explicit.
51:
52:Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures run only on explicit owner request. Do not treat the NotebookLM report as permission to run them, and do not make full feature parity or a new test suite a prerequisite for the requested implementation. Use bounded authoring/readiness/operation receipts appropriately and report what was actually checked. Preserve the existing guard/storage hold and deferred subvolume pinning.
53:
54:## Required handoff
55:
56:Update HANDOFF, SIGNALS and the existing WISHLIST entries with:
57:
58:- Current commit and exact changed files, preserving other agents' work.
59:- Methods/plugins consolidated, retired, retained for a specific local responsibility, or deferred.
60:- Canonical native targets and important argument/result/capability/state differences resolved.
61:- Build command and actual result; isolated catalog location, provenance and removal delta.
62:- Deployment status, unresolved blockers and the exact next action.
63:
64:Distinguish **proposed, implemented, built, sealed, deployed and tested**. Stop at the authorized delivery boundary. Do not claim complete consolidation, persona equivalence, successful authenticated operation or zero downtime without the corresponding evidence.
65:
66:---
67:
68:# Mastering System Consolidation — grounded implementation brief
69:
70:**Prepared:** 2026-10-18 by Codex `/root`, task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121. **Purpose:** a corrected, actionable version of the NotebookLM synthesis for another LLM to implement. This document is an implementation handoff, not a claim that consolidation has been implemented.
71:
72:**Owner decisions:** collapse handwritten functionality already owned by threetched into its native schema authority. Useful consolidation does not require full feature parity. Missing persona/configuration and memory integration features are deferred to **OD-122 and OD-123** in [WISHLIST.md](../WISHLIST.md). Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority; introduce no SQL/SQLite backend. Current access is filesystem I/O through `cognitive`; lungs becoming an MCP interface is later work, after consolidation settles.
73:
74:The original [NotebookLM webpage](<Gemini Notebook - Mastering System Consolidation_ Evidence-Backed Integration of 3tched and threetched.html>) and its supporting assets are preserved. NotebookLM synthesized supplied sources; it did not perform a live audit. This revision grounds its useful proposed sequence in mounted declarations and repository code, and labels remaining assumptions.
75:
76:## 1. Outcome and implementation scope
77:
78:The outcome is **one native contract owner for threetched functionality**, projected through our existing filesystem and admission path. A native operation should not have separately authored schemas under `threetched`, `tched_router`, `large_language_model` or another name.
79:
80:Start with a coherent, useful slice: finish the direct plugin/skill-wrapper consolidation, then migrate additional proven overlaps as their required contracts and callers are understood. Capture only the native contracts needed for the selected slice. Complete the affected source, callers, generated artifacts, mount selections and release catalog together. Do not turn the first slice into a prerequisite to implement every native tool, persona, workflow or memory feature.
81:
82:For each existing behavior, explicitly select one disposition:
83:
84:- **Migrate now:** native counterpart established; implement its canonical contract and update callers.
85:- **Keep as an integration responsibility:** identity admission, scoped context, committed-state publication or receipts still belong to our system. This does not justify independently redefining the native operation.
86:- **Defer:** record the missing feature and caller impact on the existing task board. Do not expose a fake-success operation or claim parity for deferred behavior.
87:- **Retire:** remove the declaration and reconcile its callers/policy references; document the resulting feature change.
88:
89:Removing duplicate declarations is not itself a reason to move or delete authoritative data. Preserve existing principal/session partitions and Cozo data. A compatibility name, if temporarily necessary for a demonstrated caller, must resolve to the one canonical declaration and admission path; it must not become another independently authored plugin schema or permanent wrapper layer.
90:
91:## 2. Evidence baseline
92:
93:Evidence labels used below:
94:
95:- **Mounted:** observed in the identity-bound filesystem declarations during this work.
96:- **Source:** implementation exists in the inspected checkout or pinned upstream input; this alone does not prove a successful live operation.
97:- **Proposed:** an implementation choice or sequence, not completed behavior.
98:- **Deferred/unresolved:** not established or not included in the initial delivery.
99:
100:| Baseline | Evidence |
101:|---|---|
102:| Source HEAD | `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a`, with substantial shared uncommitted work. Do not reset, stash or overwrite it. |
103:| Our mounted view | `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`: **70 plugins / 1,180 methods**. |
104:| Upstream mounted view | `/run/mounts/threetched`: **4 plugins / 208 methods**: `threetched` 147, `tched_router` 43, `tched_plugins` 6, `tched_skills` 12. |
105:| Combined inventory | **74 plugins / 1,388 method declarations**, re-counted from mounted schemas for this revision. |
106:| Catalog pin | Generation 74, hash `8a34d0da9517b137063314e07f5fa9a24fe3a3fe33920b1de2df941380041fd6`. |
107:| Native capture | Binary version **threetched 0.8.4**, plugin schema version **1.0.0**, format `threetched-cli/1`, **147 CLI operations / 83 top-level Config sections**. Binary version and plugin schema version are different fields. |
108:| Native method limits | All 147 CLI methods declare `mutation` and `idempotent=false`; their result envelope is `{stdout, stderr, exit}`. `agent` exists; **`threetched.Chat` does not**. |
109:| Existing deployment | The earlier deployment receipt records B/root304 as active, release `release-c6ece6d3-7cd5-4761-99a2-56bf684706fe`, with A/root299 previous. This report revision did not activate or independently re-certify the release. |
110:
111:Primary evidence: [mounted native schema][E1], [mounted catalog view][E2], [full overlap report][E3], [complete method inventory][E4]. The inventory is JSON content saved with a `.txt` extension for sharing; older notes referring to its `.json` filename are stale.
112:
113:The original map inventories every method; it does not establish end-to-end equivalence for all methods. It explicitly identifies missing native contracts. The NotebookLM sentence saying the map treated CLI help as proof of complete equivalence is removed by this revision.
114:
115:## 3. What to consolidate
116:
117:### Confirmed delegation and shared native implementations
118:
119:| Surface | Established relationship | Implementation implication |
120:|---|---|---|
121:| `tched_plugins` — 6 | Native `plugin.install/list/migrate/info/remove/search`. | Strong first removal candidate. Confirm arguments, output handling, exact admission and callers against the canonical native operations. |
122:| `tched_skills` — 12 | Native `skills.add/audit/edit/install/list/remove/test` and `skills.bundle.add/list/remove/rename/show`. | Same first-slice treatment. The 12 native commands are already captured. |
123:| `large_language_model` — 8 | A facade targeting **tched_router**, not eight already available native CLI replacements. Exact targets below. | Migrate callers to the derived threetched contract when the needed selection/generation operations exist. Moving router declarations into this plugin would preserve duplication. |

# Implementation prompt

Implement threetched consolidation in `/srv/git/odbus-verified`, using the grounded implementation brief included below this prompt in this same file. Read that brief in full before editing.

Read `AGENTS.md` and all its mandatory skill preloads first, then current `HANDOFF.md`, relevant `SIGNALS.md`, `WISHLIST.md`, the brief, and:

- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.md`
- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.txt` — JSON method inventory with a sharing-friendly extension.

The original NotebookLM report is a synthesis of supplied sources, not live verification. The grounded brief supersedes its unsupported endpoint names, equivalence claims and automatic test gates. Verify present code and mounted declarations before relying on dated counts or source locations.

## Objective

Collapse handwritten operations already owned by the native threetched runtime into its one native-derived plugin schema. Keep our code under the 3tched distinction and the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime under threetched. Do not relocate duplicate declarations into `large_language_model`, another plugin, a separate schema directory or a new transport shim.

Deliver working implementation and required build/catalog preparation, not another plan. Make the largest coherent, evidence-backed consolidation you can complete without speculative feature expansion. Begin with the direct plugin/skill wrappers, then continue into other established overlaps in dependency order. Explicitly record remaining work and blockers; do not describe a partial slice as complete consolidation.

Full feature parity is not required. Missing persona/configuration features are **OD-122**, and native memory integration is **OD-123**. Those are wishlist work, not prerequisites for unrelated consolidation. Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority. Introduce no SQL/SQLite backend, automatic data migration or silent memory substitution. Existing unrelated migration debt is not this task.

Current access is filesystem I/O, and the current name is **cognitive**. Lungs becomes an MCP interface after consolidation settles; do not implement that future interface here.

## Implementation requirements

1. Claim ownership in HANDOFF before editing. Preserve shared changes. The two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source, with associated module/dispatch/hash-helper edits, but that removal was not built, sealed or deployed. Reconcile and finish it; do not reset or blindly repeat it.

2. Begin with the mounted namespaces `/run/mounts/threetched` and `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`. Discover supported contracts there. Use pinned native source/export code to diagnose missing capture through the repository's supported maintenance/authoring path. Preserve caller identity and capability checks; do not bypass an absent or denied operation with another identity or transport.

3. Complete the direct-wrapper slice: map all six `tched_plugins` and twelve `tched_skills` operations to the already captured native commands; reconcile arguments/results, callers, exact capabilities, registry/module/dispatch references, generated artifacts and mount selection. The mount adapter currently lists all four upstream IDs. Catalog removal and the adapter must agree.

4. For additional config/provider/cron/router/LLM/cognitive overlap, assign every affected method a concrete disposition: migrate now, retain a genuine local integration responsibility, defer, or retire. Existing caller dependencies identify migration work; they do not justify a second native schema authority. Reconcile callers for removed or deferred behavior and expose truthful unsupported/unavailable outcomes instead of fake success.

5. Add only the native capture required for the selected operations. Extend the existing verified native export/capture and explicit `opblob` authoring boundary. Runtime continues to consume sealed blobs. Do not invent `threetched.Chat`, HTTP endpoints, WebSocket frames or native memory support. The brief contains the observed real names and source references. Missing capture does not mean a feature is absent, and a configuration section is not an HTTP endpoint.

6. Keep identity admission, private state partitions, exact grants, committed SHM publication, receipt/error semantics and cancellation outcomes intact for delivered operations. Do not globally rename state ownership or rewrite grants without tracing the affected contracts. Native stream disconnect does not prove a provider request was undone. No wildcard grants, new identity, blanket capability expansion or security-policy weakening.

7. Update demonstrated consumers across the bridge, generated surfaces, toolsets, the sibling `/srv/git/3tched.com` UI and its pinned release input where affected. A compatibility name may temporarily resolve to the canonical declaration and admission path; it must not establish a separately authored schema. Do not retain wrappers indefinitely merely to avoid migrating callers.

## Build, catalog and deployment boundary

This prompt requests a native GNU release workspace build for the resulting cross-crate change:

```sh
CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

Use the repository's existing JEV execution routing without model overrides. Run one Cargo process at a time; respect an existing build. Keep the primary agent available for source review and communication. Every delegated agent must perform its own mandatory preload and share task/file ownership.

Use the freshly built `target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/opblob` to prepare a **new isolated catalog** through `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>`, with the service's current schema-shaping environment. Review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs, retain recoverable inputs and ensure matching binaries, generated views, configuration and any affected pinned UI input. Golden consumes the presealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.

The default deliverable for this prompt is implemented source, required build results, isolated release inputs and a precise deployment handoff. If the owner separately includes live activation in the receiving task, use only the canonical `./activate-golden.sh` snapshot/send-receive path and its receipts. Never hand-copy application binaries into the live installation. Keep host mount wiring and rollback implications explicit.

Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures run only on explicit owner request. Do not treat the NotebookLM report as permission to run them, and do not make full feature parity or a new test suite a prerequisite for the requested implementation. Use bounded authoring/readiness/operation receipts appropriately and report what was actually checked. Preserve the existing guard/storage hold and deferred subvolume pinning.

## Required handoff

Update HANDOFF, SIGNALS and the existing WISHLIST entries with:

- Current commit and exact changed files, preserving other agents' work.
- Methods/plugins consolidated, retired, retained for a specific local responsibility, or deferred.
- Canonical native targets and important argument/result/capability/state differences resolved.
- Build command and actual result; isolated catalog location, provenance and removal delta.
- Deployment status, unresolved blockers and the exact next action.

Distinguish **proposed, implemented, built, sealed, deployed and tested**. Stop at the authorized delivery boundary. Do not claim complete consolidation, persona equivalence, successful authenticated operation or zero downtime without the corresponding evidence.

# Mastering System Consolidation — grounded implementation brief

**Prepared:** 2026-10-18 by Codex `/root`, task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121. **Purpose:** a corrected, actionable version of the NotebookLM synthesis for another LLM to implement. This document is an implementation handoff, not a claim that consolidation has been implemented.

**Owner decisions:** collapse handwritten functionality already owned by threetched into its native schema authority. Useful consolidation does not require full feature parity. Missing persona/configuration and memory integration features are deferred to **OD-122 and OD-123** in [WISHLIST.md](../WISHLIST.md). Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority; introduce no SQL/SQLite backend. Current access is filesystem I/O through `cognitive`; lungs becoming an MCP interface is later work, after consolidation settles.

The original [NotebookLM webpage](<Gemini Notebook - Mastering System Consolidation_ Evidence-Backed Integration of 3tched and threetched.html>) and its supporting assets are preserved. NotebookLM synthesized supplied sources; it did not perform a live audit. This revision grounds its useful proposed sequence in mounted declarations and repository code, and labels remaining assumptions.

## 1. Outcome and implementation scope

The outcome is **one native contract owner for threetched functionality**, projected through our existing filesystem and admission path. A native operation should not have separately authored schemas under `threetched`, `tched_router`, `large_language_model` or another name.

Start with a coherent, useful slice: finish the direct plugin/skill-wrapper consolidation, then migrate additional proven overlaps as their required contracts and callers are understood. Capture only the native contracts needed for the selected slice. Complete the affected source, callers, generated artifacts, mount selections and release catalog together. Do not turn the first slice into a prerequisite to implement every native tool, persona, workflow or memory feature.

For each existing behavior, explicitly select one disposition:

- **Migrate now:** native counterpart established; implement its canonical contract and update callers.
- **Keep as an integration responsibility:** identity admission, scoped context, committed-state publication or receipts still belong to our system. This does not justify independently redefining the native operation.

76:## 1. Outcome and implementation scope
77:
78:The outcome is **one native contract owner for threetched functionality**, projected through our existing filesystem and admission path. A native operation should not have separately authored schemas under `threetched`, `tched_router`, `large_language_model` or another name.
79:
80:Start with a coherent, useful slice: finish the direct plugin/skill-wrapper consolidation, then migrate additional proven overlaps as their required contracts and callers are understood. Capture only the native contracts needed for the selected slice. Complete the affected source, callers, generated artifacts, mount selections and release catalog together. Do not turn the first slice into a prerequisite to implement every native tool, persona, workflow or memory feature.
81:
82:For each existing behavior, explicitly select one disposition:
83:
84:- **Migrate now:** native counterpart established; implement its canonical contract and update callers.
85:- **Keep as an integration responsibility:** identity admission, scoped context, committed-state publication or receipts still belong to our system. This does not justify independently redefining the native operation.
86:- **Defer:** record the missing feature and caller impact on the existing task board. Do not expose a fake-success operation or claim parity for deferred behavior.
87:- **Retire:** remove the declaration and reconcile its callers/policy references; document the resulting feature change.
88:
89:Removing duplicate declarations is not itself a reason to move or delete authoritative data. Preserve existing principal/session partitions and Cozo data. A compatibility name, if temporarily necessary for a demonstrated caller, must resolve to the one canonical declaration and admission path; it must not become another independently authored plugin schema or permanent wrapper layer.

# Implementation prompt

Implement threetched consolidation in `/srv/git/odbus-verified`, using the grounded implementation brief included below this prompt in this same file. Read that brief in full before editing.

Read `AGENTS.md` and all its mandatory skill preloads first, then current `HANDOFF.md`, relevant `SIGNALS.md`, `WISHLIST.md`, the brief, and:

## 1. Outcome and implementation scope

The outcome is **one native contract owner for threetched functionality**, projected through our existing filesystem and admission path. A native operation should not have separately authored schemas under `threetched`, `tched_router`, `large_language_model` or another name.

Start with a coherent, useful slice: finish the direct plugin/skill-wrapper consolidation, then migrate additional proven overlaps as their required contracts and callers are understood. Capture only the native contracts needed for the selected slice. Complete the affected source, callers, generated artifacts, mount selections and release catalog together. Do not turn the first slice into a prerequisite to implement every native tool, persona, workflow or memory feature.

For each existing behavior, explicitly select one disposition:

- **Migrate now:** native counterpart established; implement its canonical contract and update callers.
- **Keep as an integration responsibility:** identity admission, scoped context, committed-state publication or receipts still belong to our system. This does not justify independently redefining the native operation.
- **Defer:** record the missing feature and caller impact on the existing task board. Do not expose a fake-success operation or claim parity for deferred behavior.
- **Retire:** remove the declaration and reconcile its callers/policy references; document the resulting feature change.

Removing duplicate declarations is not itself a reason to move or delete authoritative data. Preserve existing principal/session partitions and Cozo data. A compatibility name, if temporarily necessary for a demonstrated caller, must resolve to the one canonical declaration and admission path; it must not become another independently authored plugin schema or permanent wrapper layer.

5. Golden preparation stages the already sealed catalog; snapshot send/receive and activation transport it. FUSE projects the resulting declarations and committed state.

# Implementation prompt

Implement threetched consolidation in `/srv/git/odbus-verified`, using the grounded implementation brief included below this prompt in this same file. Read that brief in full before editing.

Read `AGENTS.md` and all its mandatory skill preloads first, then current `HANDOFF.md`, relevant `SIGNALS.md`, `WISHLIST.md`, the brief, and:

- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.md`
- `reports/threetched-overlap-map-20261018.txt` — JSON method inventory with a sharing-friendly extension.

The original NotebookLM report is a synthesis of supplied sources, not live verification. The grounded brief supersedes its unsupported endpoint names, equivalence claims and automatic test gates. Verify present code and mounted declarations before relying on dated counts or source locations.

## Objective

Collapse handwritten operations already owned by the native threetched runtime into its one native-derived plugin schema. Keep our code under the 3tched distinction and the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime under threetched. Do not relocate duplicate declarations into `large_language_model`, another plugin, a separate schema directory or a new transport shim.

Deliver working implementation and required build/catalog preparation, not another plan. Make the largest coherent, evidence-backed consolidation you can complete without speculative feature expansion. Begin with the direct plugin/skill wrappers, then continue into other established overlaps in dependency order. Explicitly record remaining work and blockers; do not describe a partial slice as complete consolidation.

Full feature parity is not required. Missing persona/configuration features are **OD-122**, and native memory integration is **OD-123**. Those are wishlist work, not prerequisites for unrelated consolidation. Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority. Introduce no SQL/SQLite backend, automatic data migration or silent memory substitution. Existing unrelated migration debt is not this task.

Current access is filesystem I/O, and the current name is **cognitive**. Lungs becomes an MCP interface after consolidation settles; do not implement that future interface here.

## Implementation requirements

1. Claim ownership in HANDOFF before editing. Preserve shared changes. The two direct wrapper modules were already deleted in source, with associated module/dispatch/hash-helper edits, but that removal was not built, sealed or deployed. Reconcile and finish it; do not reset or blindly repeat it.

2. Begin with the mounted namespaces `/run/mounts/threetched` and `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`. Discover supported contracts there. Use pinned native source/export code to diagnose missing capture through the repository's supported maintenance/authoring path. Preserve caller identity and capability checks; do not bypass an absent or denied operation with another identity or transport.

3. Complete the direct-wrapper slice: map all six `tched_plugins` and twelve `tched_skills` operations to the already captured native commands; reconcile arguments/results, callers, exact capabilities, registry/module/dispatch references, generated artifacts and mount selection. The mount adapter currently lists all four upstream IDs. Catalog removal and the adapter must agree.

4. For additional config/provider/cron/router/LLM/cognitive overlap, assign every affected method a concrete disposition: migrate now, retain a genuine local integration responsibility, defer, or retire. Existing caller dependencies identify migration work; they do not justify a second native schema authority. Reconcile callers for removed or deferred behavior and expose truthful unsupported/unavailable outcomes instead of fake success.

5. Add only the native capture required for the selected operations. Extend the existing verified native export/capture and explicit `opblob` authoring boundary. Runtime continues to consume sealed blobs. Do not invent `threetched.Chat`, HTTP endpoints, WebSocket frames or native memory support. The brief contains the observed real names and source references. Missing capture does not mean a feature is absent, and a configuration section is not an HTTP endpoint.

6. Keep identity admission, private state partitions, exact grants, committed SHM publication, receipt/error semantics and cancellation outcomes intact for delivered operations. Do not globally rename state ownership or rewrite grants without tracing the affected contracts. Native stream disconnect does not prove a provider request was undone. No wildcard grants, new identity, blanket capability expansion or security-policy weakening.

7. Update demonstrated consumers across the bridge, generated surfaces, toolsets, the sibling `/srv/git/3tched.com` UI and its pinned release input where affected. A compatibility name may temporarily resolve to the canonical declaration and admission path; it must not establish a separately authored schema. Do not retain wrappers indefinitely merely to avoid migrating callers.

## Build, catalog and deployment boundary

This prompt requests a native GNU release workspace build for the resulting cross-crate change:

```sh
CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
```

Use the repository's existing JEV execution routing without model overrides. Run one Cargo process at a time; respect an existing build. Keep the primary agent available for source review and communication. Every delegated agent must perform its own mandatory preload and share task/file ownership.

Use the freshly built `target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/opblob` to prepare a **new isolated catalog** through `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>`, with the service's current schema-shaping environment. Review exact added/changed/removed plugin IDs, retain recoverable inputs and ensure matching binaries, generated views, configuration and any affected pinned UI input. Golden consumes the presealed catalog via `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; it does not reseal it.

The default deliverable for this prompt is implemented source, required build results, isolated release inputs and a precise deployment handoff. If the owner separately includes live activation in the receiving task, use only the canonical `./activate-golden.sh` snapshot/send-receive path and its receipts. Never hand-copy application binaries into the live installation. Keep host mount wiring and rollback implications explicit.

Tests, Clippy, formatting checks and custom smoke fixtures run only on explicit owner request. Do not treat the NotebookLM report as permission to run them, and do not make full feature parity or a new test suite a prerequisite for the requested implementation. Use bounded authoring/readiness/operation receipts appropriately and report what was actually checked. Preserve the existing guard/storage hold and deferred subvolume pinning.

## Required handoff

Update HANDOFF, SIGNALS and the existing WISHLIST entries with:

- Current commit and exact changed files, preserving other agents' work.
- Methods/plugins consolidated, retired, retained for a specific local responsibility, or deferred.
- Canonical native targets and important argument/result/capability/state differences resolved.
- Build command and actual result; isolated catalog location, provenance and removal delta.
- Deployment status, unresolved blockers and the exact next action.

Distinguish **proposed, implemented, built, sealed, deployed and tested**. Stop at the authorized delivery boundary. Do not claim complete consolidation, persona equivalence, successful authenticated operation or zero downtime without the corresponding evidence.

# Mastering System Consolidation — grounded implementation brief

**Prepared:** 2026-10-18 by Codex `/root`, task `threetched-single-surface-20261018` / OD-121. **Purpose:** a corrected, actionable version of the NotebookLM synthesis for another LLM to implement. This document is an implementation handoff, not a claim that consolidation has been implemented.

**Owner decisions:** collapse handwritten functionality already owned by threetched into its native schema authority. Useful consolidation does not require full feature parity. Missing persona/configuration and memory integration features are deferred to **OD-122 and OD-123** in [WISHLIST.md](../WISHLIST.md). Keep **Cozo** as the storage authority; introduce no SQL/SQLite backend. Current access is filesystem I/O through `cognitive`; lungs becoming an MCP interface is later work, after consolidation settles.

The original [NotebookLM webpage](<Gemini Notebook - Mastering System Consolidation_ Evidence-Backed Integration of 3tched and threetched.html>) and its supporting assets are preserved. NotebookLM synthesized supplied sources; it did not perform a live audit. This revision grounds its useful proposed sequence in mounted declarations and repository code, and labels remaining assumptions.

## 1. Outcome and implementation scope

The outcome is **one native contract owner for threetched functionality**, projected through our existing filesystem and admission path. A native operation should not have separately authored schemas under `threetched`, `tched_router`, `large_language_model` or another name.

Start with a coherent, useful slice: finish the direct plugin/skill-wrapper consolidation, then migrate additional proven overlaps as their required contracts and callers are understood. Capture only the native contracts needed for the selected slice. Complete the affected source, callers, generated artifacts, mount selections and release catalog together. Do not turn the first slice into a prerequisite to implement every native tool, persona, workflow or memory feature.

For each existing behavior, explicitly select one disposition:

- **Migrate now:** native counterpart established; implement its canonical contract and update callers.
- **Keep as an integration responsibility:** identity admission, scoped context, committed-state publication or receipts still belong to our system. This does not justify independently redefining the native operation.
- **Defer:** record the missing feature and caller impact on the existing task board. Do not expose a fake-success operation or claim parity for deferred behavior.
- **Retire:** remove the declaration and reconcile its callers/policy references; document the resulting feature change.

Removing duplicate declarations is not itself a reason to move or delete authoritative data. Preserve existing principal/session partitions and Cozo data. A compatibility name, if temporarily necessary for a demonstrated caller, must resolve to the one canonical declaration and admission path; it must not become another independently authored plugin schema or permanent wrapper layer.

## 2. Evidence baseline

Evidence labels used below:

- **Mounted:** observed in the identity-bound filesystem declarations during this work.
- **Source:** implementation exists in the inspected checkout or pinned upstream input; this alone does not prove a successful live operation.
- **Proposed:** an implementation choice or sequence, not completed behavior.
- **Deferred/unresolved:** not established or not included in the initial delivery.

| Baseline | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Source HEAD | `051a20d056afba074e21d797aa34f8947c543c5a`, with substantial shared uncommitted work. Do not reset, stash or overwrite it. |
| Our mounted view | `/run/mounts/3tchedFS`: **70 plugins / 1,180 methods**. |
| Upstream mounted view | `/run/mounts/threetched`: **4 plugins / 208 methods**: `threetched` 147, `tched_router` 43, `tched_plugins` 6, `tched_skills` 12. |
| Combined inventory | **74 plugins / 1,388 method declarations**, re-counted from mounted schemas for this revision. |
| Catalog pin | Generation 74, hash `8a34d0da9517b137063314e07f5fa9a24fe3a3fe33920b1de2df941380041fd6`. |
| Native capture | Binary version **threetched 0.8.4**, plugin schema version **1.0.0**, format `threetched-cli/1`, **147 CLI operations / 83 top-level Config sections**. Binary version and plugin schema version are different fields. |
| Native method limits | All 147 CLI methods declare `mutation` and `idempotent=false`; their result envelope is `{stdout, stderr, exit}`. `agent` exists; **`threetched.Chat` does not**. |
| Existing deployment | The earlier deployment receipt records B/root304 as active, release `release-c6ece6d3-7cd5-4761-99a2-56bf684706fe`, with A/root299 previous. This report revision did not activate or independently re-certify the release. |

Primary evidence: [mounted native schema][E1], [mounted catalog view][E2], [full overlap report][E3], [complete method inventory][E4]. The inventory is JSON content saved with a `.txt` extension for sharing; older notes referring to its `.json` filename are stale.

The original map inventories every method; it does not establish end-to-end equivalence for all methods. It explicitly identifies missing native contracts. The NotebookLM sentence saying the map treated CLI help as proof of complete equivalence is removed by this revision.

## 3. What to consolidate

| Surface | Established relationship | Implementation implication |

| `tched_plugins` — 6 | Native `plugin.install/list/migrate/info/remove/search`. | Strong first removal candidate. Confirm arguments, output handling, exact admission and callers against the canonical native operations. |
| `tched_skills` — 12 | Native `skills.add/audit/edit/install/list/remove/test` and `skills.bundle.add/list/remove/rename/show`. | Same first-slice treatment. The 12 native commands are already captured. |
| `large_language_model` — 8 | A facade targeting **tched_router**, not eight already available native CLI replacements. Exact targets below. | Migrate callers to the derived threetched contract when the needed selection/generation operations exist. Moving router declarations into this plugin would preserve duplication. |
| `cron` — 9 | Uses native cron storage. Seven methods relate to CLI actions; history/run use native HTTP routes. | Capture only missing contracts needed for the chosen cron slice. Preserve scope and distinguish accepted backend effects from publication/receipt failure. |
| `mcp` — 3 | `get_config` and `configure_server` delegate to native config through router methods. `configure_tool_groups` is local bridge policy. | Consolidate the two config facades. Assess the remaining policy separately; its name is not an instruction to implement lungs MCP now. |
| `gemma_brain.route` | Delegates to router `ResolveRoute`. | Migrate this operation after native route resolution is mapped. This does not establish equivalence for the other 16 methods. |
| `model_registry.native_list_providers` | Reads native configuration/provider inventory and applies agent-owned-profile/selectability filtering. | Preserve the filtering when migrating. It is not a bare `providers.list` passthrough. |
| Cognitive persona consultations + `specialist` | **568** exposed methods share native provider-only completion. | Shared inference establishes a consolidation opportunity; it does not prove native agent execution reproduces the surrounding context, tools, memory and result behavior. Persona enhancements can be deferred. |

Exact LLM facade targets from [large_language_model_methods.rs][E5]: `list_providers→ListProviders`; `get_provider/get_config→GetState`; `set_provider→SetProvider`; `generate→Chat`; `stream_generate→start_generation`; `list_models→ListModels`; `update_config→SetSelection`. Every target in this sentence currently belongs to **tched_router**. Do not rename it to `threetched.<same-name>` without creating a native-derived contract and implementation.

Other evidence: [cron gateway][E6], [MCP config facade][E7], [provider inventory and filtering][E8], [specialist completion][E9].

### All 43 router methods must have a disposition

| Group | Count | Methods / mapping obligation |
|---|---:|---|
| Config/schema | 15 | `GetConfig`, `GetConfigSchema`, `GetMcpConfig`, `PatchConfig`; `config_get/init/list/migrate/patch/set`; aliases `get/init/list/patch/set`. Compare with native Config and typed config operations, including masking and coherent state observation. |
| Inventory/projection | 9 | `GetState`, `GetProviderCatalog`, `GetModelRoutes`, `GetRouter`, `GetStructuredOutput`, `GetTools`, `ListModels`, `ListProviders`, `ListUiSurfaces`. Native providers/models/config overlap; tool metadata and UI/state projections are not all represented by CLI envelopes. |
| Selection/routing/bindings | 12 | `SetModel`, `SetProvider`, `SetSelection`, five role setters (`CozoRetrieval`, `Obfuscation`, `OvsRouting`, `QdrantRetrieval`, `Vectorization`), `ResolveRoute`, `apply_catalog_model_binding`, `resolve_catalog_model_binding`, `get_own_agent_route`. Map native configuration/routing separately from local catalog bindings and caller-specific selection. |
| Generation | 7 | `Chat`, `start_generation`, `cancel_generation`, `get_generation_job`, `get_generation_jobs`, `delete_generation_job`, `recover_generation_jobs`. Native inference exists. Local jobs, revisions, publication, cancellation and recovery have separate implementation obligations. |

Evidence: [mounted router schema][E10], [router declaration source][E11], [generation job dispatcher][E12]. No requirement is imposed to reproduce every router feature in the first release. Every removed or deferred feature must nevertheless have an explicit disposition and reconciled callers.

### Coverage of the rest of the catalog

The complete 74-plugin disposition table and method names remain in [the overlap map][E3] and [machine inventory][E4]. Its classification totals are:

| Classification | Plugins | Methods | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
